The exporter ensures the configured helper version/profile is installed, writes the known activity-ID exclusion file, then starts the primary GPX export. ## Helper interfaces | Helper | Arguments | Environment | | --- | --- | --- | | garmin_export/run_export.sh | username, password, exclude file, gcexport version | venv_gcexport_<version> and gcexport_src_<version> | | garmin_fit_export/run_fit_export.sh | username, password, activity ID, save directory, optional profile (default default) | venv_fit_<profile> | install_gcexport.sh and install_fit_export.sh create the corresponding environments during the image build or through runtime tool management. The Dockerfile owns default versions and packages. The primary wrapper exports into its versioned source directory, then copies GARMIN_CONNECT_EXPORTED_TRACKS without overwriting existing files into /app/gpx/. This path is currently fixed in the wrapper. The standard Compose watcher instead uses /app/mtl-data/gpx; Garmin setup therefore needs the additional mount described in Garmin setup . The FIT fallback uses mtl.garmin-sync.fit-export-save-dir, set to the watched directory by Compose. It retains activity_<id>.fit and writes activity_<id>.gpx. See the FIT helper . ## Failure handling The intended fallback is a failed GPX download, commonly a timeout. The current parser actually selects log lines matching \[ERROR\].*?gpx/activity/(\d+); it does not require the text 408. It deduplicates the captured IDs and retries them through FIT export. A generic error with no matching activity URL cannot select an activity for retry. FIT requests can also fail. The server captures helper output and reports export duration, retry results, and errors. A completed export and completed indexing are separate milestones. Open Settings → Import & sync → Garmin for command output and Settings → Processing for indexing. Helper installation controls are under Settings → Maintenance → Advanced tools . Sync remains optional and disabled by default. Configure credentials privately; the Garmin setup guide describes the required configuration and mounts.

title: GPS architecture
text: # GPS architecture - GPS ingestion - GPS data processing pipeline - Source quality and review - Motion and break detection

title: GPS ingestion
text: # GPS ingestion The filesystem index owns source identity, detected changes, queued processing, and failures. Startup catch-up and live watching feed the same normal import path. Converters normalize supported formats before GPX parsing. Import preserves original source observations separately from the denoised canonical stream. Recorded sections, missing measurements, and timing provenance remain explicit. Canonical point metrics feed summaries and analysis. Simplified variants serve map display and reference canonical point indices. Supported observed_path geometry omits connecting recording-gap edges for spatial consumers. Import and downstream completion are distinct: duplicate classification, activity classification, energy, exploration, and media correlation have their own work states. Major operations and failures are logged with context. Diagnosis publishes common source issues for account acknowledgement, including quality findings from successfully imported tracks. Shared use settings and timing restrictions remain separate. See processing , quality ownership , and module boundaries .

title: Motion and break detection
text: # Motion and break detection MTL Explorer classifies the accepted denoised canonical observations once during import. Classification does not delete points, move coordinates, or rewrite elevation. Isolated-spike cleanup remains an earlier, separate operation. Kalman smoothing preserves runs of at least three identical accepted XYZ positions within each continuous recording section. This prevents its velocity model from introducing movement into a recorded plateau. Missing altitude stays missing. Preserving these positions does not establish a stop by itself: the timing, recording continuity and stationary-support rules below still apply. ## Stored timeline Each canonical point owns the interval [previous timestamp, this timestamp). motionState is MOVING, STOPPED, or UNKNOWN; motionReason records the evidence or missing support. The existing intervalStatus separately describes geometry and recording continuity. Uncertain motion does not erase supported geometry. The first point has no elapsed interval. Repeated timestamps supply no positive elapsed time and do not invalidate supported totals elsewhere. Precision reversals of at most one second use a temporary clamped clock for motion analysis, retaining stored observations and avoiding double-counted elapsed time. Missing or genuinely reversed clocks have PARTIAL or UNAVAILABLE motion status and null track-level duration totals. For a complete supported timeline, moving + stopped + unknown equals the recorded elapsed duration. COMPLETE means duration accounting is available; it can include unknown motion. ## Detection and retrospective boundaries 1. Reject motion inference across source recording breaks, invalid positions/times, or adjacent observations more than 60 seconds apart. Nearby or identical endpoints alone do not establish a pause. 2. Use horizontal displacement and, when available, vertical displacement over elapsed time. At least 0.5 km/h is movement evidence and cannot be absorbed into a pause. At most 0.3 km/h is potential stationary core evidence. Intermediate motion starts as unknown. 3. Require at least two supported positive-time intervals, hence three distinct recorded timestamps. A core must remain within 5 m of its time-weighted center, within a 10 m bounding diameter, and below 5 m net horizontal progress. Sample counts beyond this minimum do not determine event duration. 4. If very slow progress invalidates a larger candidate, examine its quieter portions (at most 0.05 km/h) for a compact core. This preserves a real pause after a slow approach without dividing a slow walk into artificial pauses. Unsupported slow progress stays unknown. 5. After confirming a core, revisit both boundaries. Nearby ambiguous intervals may be included within 5 m of the core and at most 60 seconds before/after it. The pass cannot cross observed movement or unsupported intervals. Only touching stationary ranges consolidate; movement or unresolved unknown time is never filled by proximity alone. 6. Store the original point indexes, an estimated start/end, confirmation time, and boundary brackets. Brackets include the ambiguous refinement span and adjacent observations. Track and recording edges are marked explicitly because the true boundary may lie outside the observed section. Brackets describe observation limits, not calibrated statistical confidence. Supported short pauses contribute to stopped time. Only final ranges of at least 60 seconds become visible break events. Categories are SHORT_STOP from 60 seconds, BREAK from 180 seconds, and LONG_BREAK from 600 seconds. trackDurationShortStoppedSecs is the subset of stopped time in episodes below 60 seconds. Break confirmation and estimated start are distinct. For example, observations showing a pause from 10 to 130 seconds can confirm a visible break at 70 seconds while retaining its estimated beginning at 10 seconds. This is offline retrospective boundary refinement; no live-stream latency is introduced. ## Consumers - Track moving/stopped/unknown summaries and detected events use the same import analysis. - Moving heart rate uses stored MOVING coverage with half-open boundaries, without another speed threshold or an event-based classification. Ordinary track and segment heart rate still include supported stationary time. - Moving average power uses both the mechanical energy and elapsed time of the same moving intervals. Total mechanical energy continues to use supported geometry; motion uncertainty alone does not remove that geometry or its energy estimate. - Segment stopped time clips the stationary intervals, including short pauses. Break count and longest visible break use detected events. - Event replacement preserves user events. Detected events carry OBSERVED_STATIONARY evidence, version, boundary brackets, and confirmation time. Numeric confidence is null; a cluster inlier ratio is not a probability that a stop occurred. - The overview explains short pauses and unknown motion. Break rows explain approximate boundaries and recording/track edges. Canonical revision hashes include motion state and analysis version. ## Limits and data lifecycle The thresholds are conservative defaults, not calibrated probabilities. GPS cannot reveal unobserved movement between sparse fixes or determine a sub-sample physical stop time exactly. Residual jitter and very slow movement near the thresholds can remain ambiguous. This stage assumes denoising is already correct; it does not attempt to identify raw indoor GPS drift. Schema change 083 adds nullable motion and boundary fields. It contains no historical backfill or migration-only service. New imports and ordinary reimports calculate motion-v2; existing derived records need reimport/recreation to receive the new timeline. This change does not deploy or reprocess existing servers. Motion tests cover supported pauses, movement, and unknown intervals. Dated outcomes remain internal verification records.

title: GPS data processing pipeline
text: # GPS data processing pipeline MTL Explorer uses Kalman smoothing by default. The canonical stream contains estimates and explicit support decisions; a smooth path does not prove that the source positions were correct. ## Import and estimation Background source assessment and import use the configurable GPSBabel allowance mtl.indexer.gps.conversion-timeout (default PT10M). Interactive review/export use their separate one-minute limit. Both conversion modes produce the same GPX content and preserve the original source; cancellation still terminates the converter. Native GPX and Java GeoJSON parsing do not use this subprocess limit. GPSBabel conversions, including review previews and import fallbacks, run outside database transactions. A source lock spans preparation and saving; diagnosis commits separately, then imported tracks and replacement changes commit atomically. Source revisions are checked before saving, and import failures are recorded after rollback. 1. FIT and other supported formats are converted upstream; GPXReader parses GPX observations with fractional timestamps, source section identity, and available fix, satellite, HDOP, VDOP, speed and source metadata. 2. RAW preserves parsed coordinates, including missing altitude/time and rejected 0,0 fixes. It is an observation trace, not a byte-level copy of the original file. Missing altitude and time serialize as JSON null. 3. Horizontal plausibility and probation reject short excursions. Probation uses the longer of its positive entry interval and the interval since the previous probation observation, with the usual 120-second time-credit cap. It does not accumulate time across a suspect cluster. This preserves strict checks for fast loggers while allowing recovery after near-duplicate fixes when normal observation spacing resumes. Equal, backward and missing entry timestamps retain their existing plausibility rules. A stable relocated cluster starts a disconnected recording span. Recording segments, clock resets and gaps over 120 seconds also break continuity. 4. ElevationObservationFilter rejects short, bounded vertical excursions independently of horizontal movement. Rejected altitude stays unknown. Persistent altitude steps remain reviewable rather than being removed on an unsupported assumption. 5. BreakStopTreatment removes isolated position spikes. It no longer detects stops or collapses stationary observations into anchor pairs. 6. Startup altitude stabilization and Kalman/RTS smoothing operate within recording spans. The transition and process noise use each actual time step; missing measurements skip the update. Source quality and large innovations increase measurement uncertainty. 7. RAW_OUTLIER_CLEANED stores the full-density canonical result. TrackMotionAnalyzer then classifies moving, stopped, and unknown intervals without changing accepted coordinates or elevation. Point metrics, duration, chart windows, peaks, energy, and events consume the stored support and motion decisions. See motion analysis . The Kalman settings are under mtl.denoise. Defaults are horizontal/vertical measurement sigmas 6/10 m and horizontal/vertical acceleration sigmas 2/0.5 m/s². The constructor fallback is also Kalman. Median remains an explicit option. Processing evidence records the selected algorithm, pipeline identifier and Kalman parameters. DOP changes relative uncertainty; it is not an error radius. ## Interval contract A point's intervalStatus describes the interval from the preceding point. | Status | Meaning | Metric support | |---|---|---| | START | First point | No preceding interval. | | OBSERVED | Positive, continuous timed observations | Distance/time; altitude-derived metrics require valid altitude. | | STOPPED | Stationary anchor support retained by the interval model | Supported elapsed time. Current imports classify stops separately with motionState; they do not create collapsed anchor pairs. | | GEOMETRY_ONLY | Nearby observations without usable elapsed time | Geometry distance; no speed, power or energy estimate. | | UNKNOWN | Recording break or unsupported connection | No connecting distance, ascent, speed or energy estimate. Positive elapsed time contributes to unknown duration. | Geometry-only support is bounded to 200 m without time, or 5 m for equal timestamps. Backward time never establishes a connecting edge. Motion inference uses a separate, stricter 60-second observation-gap limit. Moving, confirmed stopped and unknown seconds partition a complete increasing timeline. Missing time and backward clock resets cannot establish an absolute duration; their unknown length must not be interpreted as measured zero time. Missing altitude resets the vertical baseline. A shared 2 m ascent/descent gate feeds cumulative climbing, vertical rates and gravitational energy. Unsupported rates and peaks are null. Power limits also cap the accumulated energy and record energyLimited, so a plausible chart cannot hide an unbounded total. Energy remains an activity-dependent mechanical estimate calculated after classification. ## Background batches Energy, duplicate detection, activity classification, exploration, photo correlation, exercise-route association and synthetic demo health process bounded batches. A full batch with progress schedules its next batch immediately through the existing scheduler. Each callback yields its scheduler thread before the next batch; one running flag per job prevents overlap and duplicate continuation chains. Temporary DB connection acquisition failures pause duplicate/classification batches before marking a track failed. The current and later tracks remain pending and retry on the existing periodic schedule. Authentication, configuration and data errors are distinguished from temporary connection failures. Idle or failed batches stop their continuation and retry on the existing periodic schedule. Energy and demo-health idle checks default to five seconds. Energy generations, delayed energy/media retries, indexing prerequisites and the shared heavy-job guard remain in their respective workers. Exploration failures wait for its normal retry rather than immediately recalculating the same failed batch. Exercise associations commit metadata, activity changes and energy requests together before another batch runs. Shutdown checks stop new batches and leave pending records for restart. File indexers already use worker queues; remote sync, downloads and service probes keep their own schedules and limits. ## Storage and consumers | Variant | Consumers | |---|---| | RAW | Quality review and audit. | | RAW_OUTLIER_CLEANED | Authoritative point metrics, server chart buckets, energy and crossing analysis. | | SIMPLIFIED_SHAPE | Map rendering at 1, 10, 100 and 1000 m; points refer back to canonical indices. | recordingBreakBeforePointIndexes preserves both ends of discontinuities through simplification and map rendering. observed_path is a separate XY MultiLineString used by proximity, photo-route matching and exploration queries; it omits connecting gap edges. Coordinate arrays retain their stable point indices. Photo position interpolation requires an observed adjacent interval or an exact observation. Disconnected tracks are excluded from automatic Frechet matching, which assumes one continuous curve. Custom SQL written against the flat track column must use observed_path when continuity matters. Track Details charts use server buckets over canonical points, not map simplification. Main maps, point layers, the Details minimap and the GPS review map preserve recording breaks. Single-track 3D replay is unavailable across recording gaps. Crossing analysis also splits recording spans before timing. ## Review and validation Track Details → Quality → Review GPS observations loads GET /api/tracks/{trackId}/quality on demand. Original and processed paths can be toggled; selecting a review item shows its location, source evidence and possible metric impact. Reasons include rejected observations, large corrections, stationary support, unknown intervals and limited energy. The list shows up to 250 items, ranked by a heuristic impact score, not calibrated confidence. See the pipeline reliability tests and source assessment tests . Synthetic cases cover known failures and numerical consistency. Correlated GPS drift, slow movement and altitude steps can still be ambiguous. Ground-truth field evaluation is needed before claiming universal accuracy improvements. New derived fields are populated by new imports. Existing databases must be recreated/reimported to obtain complete evidence and observed paths; no legacy backfill is included in those field changes. Changeset 082 separately schedules one ordinary GPS reimport; see release upgrade instructions . ## Source diagnosis and timing provenance Source review assesses recorded evidence and processing results independently of repair. Severe timing findings are contained before temporal splitting; original timestamps remain in RAW observations. Estimated repairs retain their provenance on reimport. Untimed GPX routes can supply geometry without measured duration, speed, energy, or time-based health/photo matching. Findings mark a source as needing review; they do not automatically exclude it from the map or statistics. Saved use decisions control those exclusions. Estimated, conflicting, or otherwise unsupported timing independently restricts time-based calculations, duplicate preference, and exploration eligibility. Including a source does not convert estimated timing into measurements. See source review and the GPS quality module boundary . ## Indexer queue and recovery New and changed files become pending as soon as discovery is committed, even while imports are waiting. Processing shows Discovering while the file total is still growing, then reports progress against the committed queue. GPS and media counts describe source files, not track points or tracks inside a file. Manual rescans retry failed files even when their size and modification time are unchanged. Startup and scheduled scans recover pending work and changed files without repeatedly importing unchanged failed sources. Stable zero-byte GPS and media files are informational Skipped outcomes and are processed when their contents change. Earlier imported data stays available and is identified as retained data. Incomplete storage scans preserve imported database records. Removal stays pending until database cleanup succeeds; failures retain their operation and error. The indexer never deletes original GPS or media files. Completion writes retry temporary database failures, and a rescan can recover pending work whose worker is no longer active. When duplicate detection or activity classification cannot temporarily obtain a database connection, the batch pauses and leaves its tracks pending for the next scheduled turn. Invalid data and permanent errors keep their failure diagnostics. This retry does not increase worker threads or the database pool size. New derived fields are calculated by normal imports; legacy backfill is not the default policy. Acknowledgement semantics are described in source issues .

title: Source quality and review
text: # Source quality and review Source diagnosis and canonical processing have different responsibilities. Diagnosis reads source evidence and records findings. Processing persists cleaning actions and supported geometry in the same import transaction. Review reuses evidence for the matching source revision. Reassessment does not reimport or run a second cleaning algorithm. Missing or mismatched evidence remains unavailable. Raw observation inspection keeps original source order and timestamps. User inclusion decisions control map and statistical use. They cannot turn estimated timing into measured duration, speed, energy, or a time-based Health/media match. ## Review thresholds GpsReviewThresholds owns manual-review thresholds. REVIEW creates a pending source issue; warnings and routine findings remain informational. Assess each original source section, counting affected observations once. Coverage requires both the stated percentage and minimum count. | Evidence | Manual review threshold | | --- | --- | | Equal timestamps | Informational regardless of count; independently supported spatial anomalies are separate findings. | | Backward clock | Any timestamp more than 1 second behind the latest earlier usable timestamp. This includes cumulative reversals and a reversal across missing timestamps. | | Recording gaps | At least 12 hours; or a detected gap with at least 1 km endpoint displacement; or cumulative gap displacement of at least 1 km and 5% of supported recorded distance. Short-gap detection remains max(5 min, 10 × median positive sampling interval). | | Position or altitude smoothing | Any correction at least 200 m; or corrections at least 50 m at 1% of applicable observations and at least 10 points. | | Removed position spikes | Jump at least 1 km; or rejection of 1% of source observations and at least 10 points. | | Removed altitude spikes | Spike at least 300 m; or rejection of 1% of altitude observations and at least 10 points. | | Weak source fix | At least 10% of position observations, or a supported contiguous weak period of at least 5 minutes. Horizontal and vertical findings at the same point count once. | | Missing/invalid activity timestamps | At least 1% of source observations and 10 points, or all activity timestamps missing. Intentional untimed routes remain informational. | | Invalid coordinates | At least 1% of source observations and 10 points, or no usable positions. | | Empty/unreadable source | Zero observations, zero bytes, or whole-source read/conversion/parsing failure. Assessment resource limits alone remain informational. | Retained abrupt position discontinuities keep their contextual detector: at least 200 m and 50 m/s, exceeding surrounding supported speed by more than six times. Edges require at least 125 m/s and stronger available-side support. An unresolved detected discontinuity requires review. Missing optional fields and fragment count alone do not create a manual review task. Generated timing and inconsistent processing results retain their safeguards. A backward-clock alert alone does not disable a section's timing. Whole-section containment requires at least three independent backward transitions greater than one second covering at least 1% of source observations, a backward lag of at least 12 hours, or an unresolved large date excursion. Affected observations below an earlier clock maximum are not counted as independent transitions. An isolated forward clock spike requires review as one incident. Import excludes only its derived timestamp when two neighbouring supported intervals establish a consistent return: each interval is positive and at most 120 seconds; the return spans at most 240 seconds and three times their maximum cadence; the spike exceeds both neighbours by more than one second and ten times that cadence. Missing context or smaller ambiguous peaks remain source evidence. Original timestamps remain in RAW. Persisted containment evidence keeps timing unsupported after reassessment until a successful reimport rebuilds it. Unsupported local intervals still make aggregate motion partial; retaining other source timestamps does not invent complete motion totals. Aggregate changes in distance, ascent or descent after processing do not create review findings. Routine denoising can substantially change those totals. Individual correction magnitudes, rejection coverage and retained discontinuities remain assessed. Reassessment ignores stored aggregate-impact summaries, resolving their stored issues even when assessment is incomplete. Other unchecked findings remain active. It classifies current cleaning actions against source observations; it does not rerun the cleaner. New imports record the thresholds and processing version. Existing motion totals and missing cleaning evidence require ordinary reimport to rebuild. Equal timestamps retain geometry within the same 200 m support bound as untimed observations. Their instantaneous speed remains unknown. The motion analyzer retains supported totals and uses a temporary monotonic timeline for clock precision reversals of at most one second, without modifying stored observations. Diagnostics is a named module; the repair module has been removed. The Spring Boot application remains the assembly. General multi-module extraction is a separate proposal. User procedures are in Source review ; launch requirements are in GPS quality modules . ## Assessment limits and clock alerts Assessment has limits of 64 MiB and one million observations. The streaming parser retains observations and supported fields without building a document tree for device extensions. Nesting, field length, and retained review data have additional limits; unused extension elements do not consume the retained-data budget. An incomplete assessment is reported without treating the file as healthy or automatically excluding it. Original downloads are streamed without this limit; converted GPX downloads are bounded by it. All diagnosis runs on the server. Import also checks each source section for conflicting clocks when full assessment cannot finish. A backward-time alert keeps the section's supported timing. Systemic clock problems disable timing for the affected section while retaining original observations, timestamps, and geometry. A clearly isolated forward clock spike excludes only that point's derived timestamp and appears as one incident; original timestamps remain available in RAW. Recognized timing problems remain visible after reassessment. Abrupt retained relocations are checked against the surrounding pace. Endpoints use a stricter check with support from the available side. Unsupported connections become separate spans before smoothing; their connecting distance and speed do not contribute to statistics. Sustained fast travel alone does not trigger this check. Changes in total distance, ascent, or descent after smoothing do not trigger review; large individual corrections and substantial point rejection do. Updating the server does not reassess existing findings. Reassess current file applies current criteria, removes earlier aggregate-impact findings, and reuses stored cleaning evidence only when its source revision matches. It preserves existing timing containment; an ordinary reimport is required to rebuild timing, motion totals, and missing processing evidence. Without import evidence, cleaning remains Not assessed . Review does not edit, replace, or back up source files. Backup files from earlier versions remain on disk and can be managed outside the app.

title: Google Health OAuth
text: # Google Health OAuth ## Decision MTL Explorer supports a user-owned Google Cloud project in Testing status. The user adds the Google account that holds the health data as a test user and creates a Desktop app OAuth client. Testing-mode refresh tokens expire after seven days. MTL Explorer must treat regular reauthorization as part of the normal product flow, not as an unusual error. Testing is the permanent setup, not a temporary step: users do not publish the app, move it to In production , or have it verified by Google. ## Supported authorization flow - Request offline access with PKCE S256, a random single-use state, and prompt=consent. - Redirect to the dead loopback address http://127.0.0.1:1/mtl-explorer-oauth. - Tell the user that the browser error is expected. - Accept the complete address copied from the browser. Validate its host, port, authorization result, and state before exchanging the code. - Use the same redirect URI for authorization and token exchange. - Read refresh_token_expires_in from the authorization-code token response when Google supplies it. Store the calculated expiry with the connection and return it in connection status. - Encrypt the refresh token at rest and keep access tokens in memory. The complete URL is required. Unlike a bare authorization code, it lets MTL Explorer validate the OAuth state. ### Why loopback and manual return Google Desktop clients allow HTTP loopback callbacks, not arbitrary LAN or remote server URLs. localhost / 127.0.0.1 refers to the browser's device, which may differ from the MTL Explorer host. Detecting the GUI's browser URL cannot bypass this restriction. The unused loopback address and manual paste let NAS and remote installations connect without a local helper or HTTPS setup. Automatic return to a remote server requires a Web application client with an exactly registered HTTPS callback; non-loopback IP addresses are rejected. See Google's Desktop redirect rules and Web redirect rules . ### Token storage and recovery The refresh-token encryption key is derived from the configured OAuth client secret, which stays outside the database. This protects a database-only copy; it does not protect against access to both the database and server secrets. Changing the client secret makes existing ciphertext unreadable. Reauthorize after changing it; mirrored records are retained. The access-token refresh handler logs decryption failures and marks the connection for reconnection. An unreadable token can also indicate corruption, so the UI must not claim a client-secret change as the only cause. ### Advanced proxy callback The optional Web-client callback accepts an unauthenticated GET because the return from Google cannot carry the browser's MTL Explorer authorization header. An authenticated request must first create the random state and server-held PKCE verifier. The callback consumes that state once, within ten minutes, before exchanging a code. Missing, expired, or replayed state cannot change the connection. The manual completion endpoint remains authenticated. ## Reauthorization contract The initial setup must explain that the user will normally reconnect every seven days. MTL Explorer must then: 1. If Google reports a refresh-token expiry, show it as soon as setup finishes and use it to schedule an Admin action before authorization is lost. Do not invent an expiry when Google omits the field. 2. Detect an expired or revoked refresh token and set RECONNECT_REQUIRED. The timer may provide an earlier reminder, but an OAuth failure remains authoritative. 3. Classify an invalid_grant close to the recorded expiry as a likely Testing-mode expiration. Other causes, including revocation, remain possible and must not be hidden. 4. Show an action-needed notification using the existing Admin overview and Import & sync status patterns. 5. Provide a direct Reauthorize action and prepare a new Google consent link. Do not send the user through the complete setup assistant again. 6. Reuse the configured client ID and client secret. The user only completes Google consent and pastes the returned loopback URL. 7. Require a new refresh token when recovering from RECONNECT_REQUIRED; never fall back to the token known to be invalid. 8. Replace the stored token, clear any cached access token, clear the error, keep the local mirror and track associations, and start synchronization. An expiry warning can say: > This Google authorization expires on September 8 because the OAuth project > appears to be in Testing. Reauthorize Google to keep syncing. The supported action is Reauthorize . Moving the project to In production is not supported. Reauthorization must not delete or duplicate the connection, mirrored health records, imported routes, or user-owned track data. ## Reliability invariants - Resolve users/me/identity after authorization and persist its stable healthUserId. Refuse a different account when the mirror contains records, source metadata, synchronization audits/work, or retained route ownership. - Use one time domain for both a Google window and its authoritative deletion. Exercise uses civil start time; physical records use instants; daily rollups use dates. Offset and daylight-saving changes must not move records outside the replacement window. - Persist a rotated refresh token returned during access-token refresh while holding the same refresh lock. - On 401, or Google's structured MISSING_OAUTH_SCOPE response, invalidate the cached access token and retry once. Do not treat every 403 as stale authorization; distinguish missing scope, project policy, and disabled API. - Persist pagination progress. Stop an incomplete window when a page token repeats or the configured page limit is reached. Never run authoritative deletion for an incomplete window. - Only structured INVALID_PAGE_TOKEN responses restart a historical token traversal with smaller bounds. Other 400s remain request failures. Work retries are durable; exhausted ranges park without authorizing deletion or final marks. - Validate every successful page before persistence: the root must be an object, collections must be arrays of objects, page tokens must be bounded strings, and a page must not exceed the requested result limit. A missing collection remains valid because ProtoJSON normally omits empty repeated fields; {} can therefore be a legitimate empty Google response and cannot be rejected as malformed. - Honor both delta-seconds and HTTP-date forms of Retry-After, with bounded retry delays. - Log job and phase lifecycle, bounded progress milestones, final counts, and durations at INFO. Keep page-level detail and repeated recoverable stack traces at DEBUG. Log recoverable exceptions once with safe context and log terminal failures at ERROR with the throwable. - Report current-pass progress separately from the local mirror summary. The server calculates the exact unique row count and earliest/latest record time across both mirror tables. The database projection remains in the persistence package and is mapped to a separate web response DTO. Mirror-wide aggregate queries for status, per-type summaries, and sources are cached for five minutes while work is active, refreshed as soon as a new job completes, and invalidated when the mirror is deleted. See synchronization for work policies and checkpoints.

title: Google Health demo generator
text: # Google Health demo generator Technical notes for the synthetic health data used by MTL Explorer demos. Account connection and live Google synchronization are unavailable in demo mode. The generator requires both mtl.demo-mode=true and mtl.demo-health.enabled=true. Demo deployment templates enable it for every image channel; ordinary installations leave it disabled. On startup it waits for indexing and track calculations, then asynchronously checks the ordinary Health tables and fills missing records. Settings → Processing shows its progress. INFO logs show startup, waiting, missing-day counts, generation batches and completion. Failed batches are retried. Tracks and the daily overview share one fictional wearable timeline. Overlapping tracks use the same samples; the strongest effort at each timestamp supplies the workload without counting overlapping activity twice. Heart rate follows speed, available elevation and cycling power, with delayed effort response, recovery, daily variation and small correlated fluctuations. Missing elevation means flat terrain. Recording gaps are not filled. Motorized tracks generate modest heart rates and no exercise steps or active calories. Three mathematical walking, running and cycling GPX routes provide exercise examples. Daily records include steps, distance, active calories, sleep stages, resting heart rate and weight. Daily rollups cover the demo track history and at least the recent period; detailed daily heart rate is generated for the last 90 days by default, with older samples generated along tracks. Samples and raw records identify their synthetic source. No account, tokens or Google synchronization are simulated. ## Configuration | mtl.demo-health setting | Default | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | enabled | false | Explicit demo-only opt-in | | track-percentage | 100 | Stable selection from 0–100%; approximate below 100% | | seed | 20261003 | Reproducible model and selection | | sample-interval-seconds | 15 | Shared timeline sample spacing, 5–60 seconds | | batch-size | 25 | Maximum days per pass and track IDs per query | | recent-days | 90 | Minimum daily history and detailed sample generation | | run-schedule | PT1S | Delay between active passes | The percentage selects tracks that influence the fictional profile. Shared samples can also match unselected tracks when their timestamps fall within the detailed daily history or overlap a selected track. ## Implementation The Java code lives in googlehealth.demo. It uses the regular GPS and Health tables and the same typed JSON payloads as imported records, so shared Health queries can read generated metrics. It adds no schema, tables or persisted job checkpoints. Existing Health records determine which days need completion; a daily heart-rate summary includes the sample count so missing samples can be detected. Completeness checks group stored sample counts by day once across the requested period. Workloads are combined in memory, with cleaned points loaded one track at a time. Completed days are left alone, and the startup job stops when all required records exist. Generated metric payloads use the shared HealthMetricPayload Java records and the same per-data-type JSON envelope as imported measurements. The metric reader uses these records too. The demo's missing-sample check reads the nested heartRate.sampleCount field. Health queries and calculations have no generator dependency. Screen labels use the general demo status. Configuration changes affect newly filled records; recreate the demo database to regenerate a complete dataset with new settings. ## Screenshots See the capture notes for data sources and image preparation.

title: Google Health synchronization
text: # Google Health synchronization Google Health is a read-only local mirror. One serialized worker runs fixed-rate cycles, normally every 30 minutes. Busy ticks are skipped. Each cycle has a new sync ID and a deadline one minute before the next nominal tick. Manual sync, reload, and retry use the same guard, budgets, request limiter, and durable cooldown. Scheduling deadlines stop new requests. Complete batches save under the separate database timeout, even across a stream or cycle deadline. Records, checkpoints and historical rotation commit atomically before yielding; batch sizes are unchanged. Historical finalization is a separately admitted transaction. A cycle may overrun while its current batch finishes; busy ticks still create no new job. | | Recent | History | | --- | --- | --- | | Ownership | Non-final days from the seven-day cutoff onward | Eligible unmarked days before the cutoff, down to the configured floor | | Work | Last physical 24 hours first; frozen full-window pass due 24 hours after completion | Newest unmarked day first; bounded empty ranges may widen | | Commit | Validate a complete chunk before upsert and exact-range replacement | Commit batch upserts and page checkpoints; finalize each logical day from completed work | | Failure | Durable waiting/skipped cells; expired cells hand over to history | Durable waiting/parked parents; revoked workers cannot commit or finalize | Both lanes have reserved time and may borrow unused capacity. Pending full and reload work has a positive reservation inside recent time. Route exports have a bounded turn inside that reservation. Fast-first work does not create extra jobs or continuation chains. A completed full pass records its next due time; another pass starts at its new cutoff rather than the old pass's end. Temporary provider/network errors and transient database failures retain WAITING work. From the fourth failure, the normal sync interval doubles per failure with up to 20% added jitter, capped at work-retry-max-delay (six hours). Validation and other non-recoverable failures retain the four-attempt skipped/parked limit. Routes use the same policy; a failed route without a retry time needs explicit retry. Quota cooldowns, budget yields and cancellation consume no work attempt. Full recent passes advance past temporary cells in slow retry and finish with errors, retaining their waiting gaps. Fast refreshes and later full passes retry those gaps when eligible, so one failing stream cannot block new shared passes. Reload parents inherit the cell's failure state and retry time without counting another failure while the cell waits. Committed historical pages survive retries. Unrecoverable pagination-token errors retain their immediate parking after token recovery fails. Successful work clears its active error and retry time; earlier failed-attempt audits remain history until the local mirror is deleted. Physical instants, civil components, and calendar dates retain their native query keys. Civil queries cover UTC−12 through UTC+14 at both ends. Date queries cover whole native days, including the upper civil date. Requests and checkpoints use microsecond precision. Exercise ownership uses civil start; sleep ownership uses UTC end day. Sleep charts still group whole sessions by their start day in the viewing time zone. A rejected upper envelope is a failure, never an empty success. Named points retain Google identity, including heart-rate samples. Nameless raw identity includes canonical observations and source metadata; differing same-time observations survive. Nameless reconciled and rollup keys use native intervals. Identical duplicates collapse; conflicting duplicates invalidate a complete query. Historical pages are normalized once before their guarded transaction resolves sources and writes bounded multi-row INSERT … ON CONFLICT batches. Unchanged rows are not rewritten. Automatic history performs no membership stamping, pre-write changed-count scan, missing-record sweep, or completion-time mirror scan. Write results supply changed counts; stamp and deletion counts stay zero. Named heart-rate records use a partial unique index on connection and identity; timestamp corrections still update one row. Nameless identities include their physical time and content, so their partial unique index starts with connection and sample time before identity. Recent and maintenance lookups include that time. Record keys and logical uniqueness stay unchanged. The time prefix avoids scattered reads across the whole history during an import. Mirror fingerprint indexes are no longer maintained; lookups use identity and native time. Content-independent identities retain a bounded identity/fingerprint map in history_child.query_fingerprints, committed with the page checkpoint. Resumed queries restore it; restarted, revoked, and completed queries discard it. Nameless raw identities already include content and need no separate conflict map. Historical data is treated as fixed. One successful history_audit record per account, stream, representation, calendar policy, key policy, and native day is the completion authority. All required queries and pages must succeed before the audit and work completion commit together. Valid returned counts distinguish DATA from EMPTY; an unchanged existing record still counts as data. Measurement gaps are valid. An empty result does not delete local rows. Bounded empty-range queries still produce a separate completion record for each day. Each cycle keeps a search position per stream and reuses its selected day when creating work. The position moves backward only after that selected work and its day audits commit. Completing older work resumed from another cycle does not move it past newer gaps. A completed stream needs one gap search per cycle; saved retries remain eligible after the search is exhausted. Positions reset every cycle, and ownership guards still reject work revoked by reload. Audits remain the completion authority. The cycle log's historyGapSearches counts these gap queries, separately from provider requests. Automatic sync skips successful days permanently, including after restart or a wider recent window. Explicit range/all reload supersedes matching marks and revokes overlapping work without pre-deleting records. A durable RELOAD_REQUESTED audit records the requested range; new historical work sets replace_missing and retains maintenance stamping and replacement, including recent-to-history handoff. Request audits do not count as completion. Unrequested parked portions retain their state under new owners. Retry releases incomplete work without reopening successful days. Reset clears mirror, audits, work, failures, passes, ownership, and caches. Empty audits and retained owners protect account identity. Route ownership is separate from mirror points. Valid exports use atomic file publication and keep their indexing associations. Recent replacement and explicit reload update absent exercise presence while retaining its file, owner, and track. Track replacement also updates absent owners. Adding location access exports stored missing routes without reopening history. Automatic synchronization never removes published route files; file deletion is confined to confirmed administration actions. Status separates cycle counts from cumulative pass/traversal counts. It reports fast bounds and completion, frozen full positions and due time, skipped/handed-over chunks, parked ranges, and contiguous history finalized back to the first gap. The Processing screen separates Recent, History, and Routes, with searchable data-type disclosures and persistent expansion across cycle transitions. Growing cycle totals use indeterminate activity; incomplete or paused work cannot appear as a completed refresh. Mirror totals and history coverage carry snapshot times. Coverage snapshots are bounded and cached; status polling does not reload all audits each time. Shared client count timelines animate confirmed count changes, settle completed cycles, and reset for each new sync ID. Active Data & Records, Processing, and service views share one status request every eight seconds. Reopening a view reuses the same in-memory snapshot and animation timeline. Overview opens with only the grouped chart query. It reads any existing shared status without requesting or polling it. Expanding Latest values loads the per-type date bounds and latest measurements; successful results are reused until the screen closes or a shared sync update makes them stale. Closing the section discards pending results and prevents follow-up requests. Overview does not fetch catalogue counts for its footer. Health screen loaders track their own requests. Shared sync updates refresh Overview charts and expanded latest values. Data & Records refreshes records, summaries, and sources without invalidating an in-flight status retry. Closing a screen invalidates all of its pending results. Record list and detail responses expose an optional typed measurement with a required numeric value and unit, plus optional minimum and maximum. Values use the chart units. The server derives valueSummary from that same measurement and preserves numeric zero. Unsupported or unavailable measurements omit the typed value. OpenAPI defines the response and generated client types. List queries project only measurement operands for the selected page. The full provider payload remains available in record details for diagnostics. The heart-rate covering-index migration drops a leftover index before retrying its concurrent build. A recorded successful original migration keeps its index; its original checksum remains valid. There is no legacy backfill or identity migration. Successful audit marks stay authoritative. An incomplete checkpoint without query-validation state restarts its subdivision under new ownership without deleting committed records. Legacy route columns remain inactive. The implementation plan contains the acceptance gate. Real-account density, upper-envelope acceptance, first-seen delays, and comparative request/byte costs still need measurements; synthetic checks do not establish a production freshness or speed guarantee. See authorization and the user guide . ## Chart grouping The grouped metrics endpoint supports AUTO, SECOND, DAY, WEEK, MONTH, and YEAR. SECOND accepts one local calendar day using the same inclusive start date, exclusive end date, and viewing time zone as the calendar groupings. This includes 23-hour and 25-hour daylight-saving days. The overview labels SECOND as Intraday . Heart rate reuses the repository's time buckets with a one-second interval. Timestamped weight, body fat, body temperature, and blood glucose readings are grouped by second after conversion to display units. Both retain average, minimum, and maximum in detailedPoints, with the selected day's summary in buckets. Daily values are not substituted for missing samples. The same chart component draws the time series and breaks a line where the gap between readings exceeds three times the series' median reading spacing, so devices that record every few seconds or minutes still draw a line. Readings with no neighbor within that spacing are drawn as markers. The overview owns one time window and one marked time for all intraday graphs. The time window control, drag selection, and pinch update that shared window without another metrics request; each graph applies it to its axis without rebuilding its series. Selecting a point marks that time on every graph, and each graph shows its nearest reading within the gap spacing. The window and mark are kept when expanding a graph and reset when a different day or grouping loads. A daily measurement graph offers the selected day as an intraday view. ## Setting constraints The settings are listed in Google Health setup . The fast window must be at least the sync interval and no longer than the physical recent window. Duration settings must be positive. recent-window covers at least two whole days, cycle-deadline-margin stays smaller than the interval, and history-budget-fraction stays strictly between zero and one. Explicit history-start-date values are preserved. Request spacing is one second across pages, probes, retries, and route exports. Provider cooldowns persist across restarts. Civil offsets are limited to UTC−12 through UTC+14; the earlier parser's ±18-hour range is no longer accepted. cursor-overlap, initial-window, and daily-reconciliation-history are retired. Daily/monthly reconciliation schedules and automatic continuations are removed. The default history floor changed from 1970 to 2010; it is a configured limit, not Google's earliest available date. The current layout targets fresh mirrors; existing checkpoints and route state from earlier development builds are not migrated or silently discarded.

title: Map exploration interactions
text: # Map exploration interactions The 2D map uses one dispatcher for exploration. Layers supply targets; the shared content sheet presents them. Drawing, measurement, and planning retain their own gestures. The separate 3D replay map does not use this dispatcher. ## Small dispatcher contract mapInteractionDecision.ts defines the target union, semantic identity, pointer/touch tolerance, deduplication, and presentation decisions. mapInteractionCoordinator.ts owns click lifetime and incremental source state. Neither module imports Vue or MapLibre at runtime. Map consumers register with registerConsumer, which returns a cleanup function. The controller exposes registerMapInteractionConsumer for additional map components; registrations can precede map initialization and survive renderer recreation until their component calls cleanup. Map children can use useMapInteractionConsumer to access the provided dispatcher and clean up on unmount: - A local consumer collects candidates synchronously from the captured click. - An asynchronous consumer supplies a cancellable provider with a bounded timeout. - Either consumer can declare eligibility against the captured context. Registration and cleanup invalidate an existing interaction. The main map adapter registers the fixed POI, track-point, photo, filtered-track, Swiss-route, and enabled Waymarked activity consumers. This is a candidate dispatcher; existing type-specific handlers still open details and photo collections. Adding a consumer does not require another map click listener or presentation surface. useMapInteractions.ts binds the dispatcher to map events and existing handlers. useMainMapController.ts binds invalidation to tool ownership, track filter revision, media scope, and layer settings. Map2DRenderer.vue hosts one exploration BottomSheet and a separate foreground GPS detail BottomSheet; MapTargetChooser.vue starts with a bounded All overview. mapTargetCategories.ts groups presentation by target kind and trail source, without changing consumer registration or candidate identity. Waymarked activities share one category, as do Swiss route layers. Unknown registered sources remain accessible through their own category. All is the initial chooser view. A ten-row preview budget shares space across categories, with at most three targets in each category, followed by a counted more row. Small sets within those bounds show every target directly. Categories with results, pending lookups or lookup issues stay reachable through wrapping, persistent chips. A summary or chip opens 20 targets per page, with every returned target accessible. Photo counts distinguish collection targets from individual photos. Pending, unavailable, and cancelled categories remain visible; completed empty categories are hidden. Available screen distances rank an initial batch. GPS peers use available server proximity distances, then canonical recording time, newest first. Localized display dates are never parsed; equal or unavailable values keep supplied order. Late arrivals preserve previews, category order, the current page, and focus. A new click resets navigation; selected content remains mounted through Back to results and reopening its result row. Category controls appear only in the chooser; selected details use the shared sheet's header Back action. The sheet's optional backLabel and back event keep navigation with the caller. Track details emit the same generic event without knowing their return destination. GPS rows share TrackChoiceRow with the photo activity picker. The row contains a title and compact activity/date/distance/ascent facts, plus available photo counts. Canonical timestamps and measurements are formatted reactively through the app's locale/unit helpers; total lengthMeters is distinct from hit distanceMeters. TrackChoiceFacts provides the compact metric badges for archived GPS rows. Proximity distances are used for ordering and are not displayed in these map lists. Its lazy cached TrackShapePreview appears on the right, before the chevron, only when the list container is at least 40 rem wide. A track icon remains on the left at every width. The sketch uses a subdued theme-aware blue, a 1.75 px stroke and no opacity fade. Mouse/pen hover and keyboard focus reuse the existing track-highlight source without changing selection, viewport or URL. Leaving the row, hiding the chooser, changing the click or closing it clears the preview while retaining the selected track highlight. Routine geometry refreshes retain an eligible preview. Touch does not preview. The chooser uses a fixed shared-sheet detent capped at 30 rem or 60% of the viewport, whichever is smaller. Its height stays constant through source updates, category changes and paging. Manual dragging and maximization remain available. GPS details open at the expanded 92vh detent and standard width on desktop. On mobile they maximize to 100dvh and full width. GPS details use a separate foreground sheet. The dispatcher stays mounted at its unchanged height, with its chooser inert while covered. Foreground opening covers at least the underlying sheet's height; explicit detail resizing is still allowed. Back, Close and browser Back hide GPS details and reveal the unchanged dispatcher, preserving its category, page and manual size. Retained GPS content stays mounted for reopening. GPS Close uses the sheet's deferClose and close-request contract to request the same return navigation as Back. The panel closes only after navigation commits. Pending or failed returns preserve its size and maximized state; Close can be retried. Drag-to-close restores the pre-drag height while waiting for navigation. Other detail types retain the dispatcher's current panel size. The chooser adds no scroll container or independent height calculation. Standalone GPS details also open expanded. When a tool such as Statistics or Filter opens GPS details, route synchronization keeps the originating tool open underneath. The return target retains its navigation state; returning reveals the existing panel without reopening it. The GPS sheet shares its layout with nested media viewers only in map exploration. Statistics, Filter and direct-link media viewers keep their own viewport centering and size presets. Ordinary media viewing leaves the GPS sheet's height unchanged; the compact background detent is enabled only while 3D replay is active. ## Lifetime and presentation Every accepted exploration click opens Choose what to see here on All, even with zero or one candidate. Only explicit row selection opens details. Pending categories show a spinner and one skeleton row while known hits remain clickable. Completed empty categories have no chip or All-list group. If the selected category finishes empty, the chooser returns to All and focuses its chip. A confirmed empty location shows “Nothing found here”; unavailable and cancelled sources remain distinct. Filtered track proximity and route identification settle independently. GPS lookup starts existing ID and nearby-media lookups in parallel. IDs and processing notices appear immediately; optional facts enrich existing rows without changing their order or selection. Media facts have a bounded three-second timeout; failure keeps GPS IDs and processing notices without reporting missing facts as zero. Late hits append without changing category navigation, visible ordering or selected details. A point's parent track remains an action of the point rather than another overlap row. Photo and cluster taps publish the primary collection and one captured Map view at tap choice directly under Photos. Fully known equal ID sets are deduplicated; incomplete cluster membership retains both scopes. Collection counts do not sum overlapping photo totals. Each row opens the existing viewer directly, with no secondary photo chooser or associated-GPS lookup in this dispatcher flow. Viewport selection uses captured IDs without expanding cluster leaves. Both scopes carry the original map bounds for the viewer's overview; legacy callers retain their existing collection chooser and current-map fallback. Full GPS details use the existing /track/:id route. useMapInteractionTrackRoute keeps the return context in the caller, separate from the dispatcher and detail components. Header Back and browser Back restore retained chooser navigation; Forward restores the same selected content. Reload or a direct link uses standalone track routing, with Back returning to an available overview or the map. Only track identity goes in the URL, and superseded or rejected navigation cannot restore an old selection. Points and photo/POI/public-route results retain the map URL until the user explicitly opens full GPS details. Each accepted click captures coordinates, actual pointer/touch/pen input, filter revision, media scope, and eligibility. Requests check both interaction identity and cancellation. Manual movement cancels unfinished discovery but retains the original click, collected targets, and selected detail loads. Programmatic focus movement preserves discovery. Double-click zoom skips the second exploration click and clears only the gesture's interaction. useMapInteractionVisibility listens to the shared sheet's actual layout. Once its opening geometry settles, an occluded click gets the minimum vertical pixel pan needed to leave 32 px above the chooser. Zoom, bearing and pitch stay fixed; the original discovery context is retained. A clear marker requires no movement. Each click gets one attempt, including clicks while the chooser stays open. Manual movement, early sheet resizing, selection and close cancel that attempt; late results, category changes and returning from details do not move the camera. Providers time out after 15 seconds. Failure, timeout, cancelled discovery, incomplete track processing, and confirmed empty results remain distinct. One failed consumer does not discard other results. Close, a new click, invalidation, style replacement, and disposal prevent late responses from reopening content. Ending retained results also discards GPS details hidden by Back to results ; they must not reopen as standalone content. Visible GPS details may continue on their standalone route when the discovery context is invalidated. For retained photo-cluster targets, the media overlay keeps the original source tree until the interaction ends. Viewport refreshes queue their latest data during that interval. This preserves collection identity and pagination after panning; no complete leaf expansion is needed. Invalidation closes a photo collection whose pagination depended on that retained tree. ## Public trail details waymarkedTrailProvider.ts captures the click tolerance through public map unprojection before any request. It intersects the frozen Mercator footprint with Waymarked Trails geometry tiles and resolves every matched top-level relation through list/by_ids. This avoids the area endpoint's 100-result cap. Adjacent tiles and repeated segments are deduplicated. Metadata requests use batches rather than limiting the number of targets. Geometry requests are limited to 16 tiles per activity and use a bounded five-minute memory cache. Wider clicks show Zoom in to identify Waymarked Trails routes , with unavailable status rather than an empty result. Names, references, itineraries, known network labels, and official route-page links appear in the existing flow. swissRouteDetails.ts fetches htmlPopup only after a Swiss feature is selected. It extracts the published SchweizMobil stage and full-route URLs from inert markup. Stage details is the primary link when present. Unnamed swisstopo segments expose available classification and a Swiss map link; missing names or homepages are not invented. Selected detail requests have a timeout and interaction/selection guards, and ordinary panning preserves them. The grouped chooser has no archive actions. Download and 3D replay remain in selected archived track content. MapOverlayDetails.vue displays only external route fields and validated links. Selected routes use a dedicated detail layout in that same sheet: a wrapped route name, activity icon, metadata card and primary external action. The first available validated link is primary, with Swiss stage details preferred. MapPoiDetails.vue presents mapped place types with their existing category icons and colors, plus elevation when available. Its pure presentation helper also supplies the sheet header icon. Both use the shared compact desktop width and content fitting. These panels add no lookups or extra sheets. API contracts: Waymarked geometry , route listings , Swiss HTML popups .

title: Map Server Flow
text: # Map Server Flow > [!NOTE] > For installation and local maps, see Map services . ## Design Principles 1. Hosted by default - normal app and demo deployments use the hosted PMTiles service through the Java backend proxy. 2. Local sidecar is optional - Docker Compose keeps map-server visible under the local-maps profile. It is not started by default. 3. No baked map archives - the mytraillog-maps image contains nginx, the PMTiles CLI, and the orchestrator only. Map data lives on the /data volume or is prepared at runtime. 4. Versioned tile files - every tile file is named by its Protomaps build date: YYYYMMDD.pmtiles. 5. Stable symlinks - planet.pmtiles and world-lowzoom.pmtiles are symbolic links pointing to the latest complete versioned files. 6. Sentinel files - a .done file next to a versioned tile means it is complete. Symlinks are created only after the sentinel exists. 7. Resume safety - on restart, the orchestrator resumes an incomplete YYYYMMDD.pmtiles version instead of switching to a newer build. 8. Java proxy owns upstream choice - the browser calls /mtl/api/map-proxy/prod/... for both hosted and local PMTiles. The backend chooses local sidecar when healthy, otherwise hosted. --- ## Build Time docker-build-deploy.py builds and pushes the map image like any other image. It no longer probes Protomaps builds and no longer passes map build arguments. The Dockerfile builds one lightweight runtime image: - Alpine - nginx - python3 - pmtiles CLI - orchestrator scripts - entrypoint No /data-prebuilt directory is copied into the image. --- ## Container Startup ### entrypoint.sh The entrypoint directly execs: ### orchestrator.py 1. Sets os.umask(0) so created files are manageable from mounted volumes. 2. Installs signal handlers for SIGTERM and SIGINT. 3. Starts nginx on port 8081. Docker health checks can pass immediately. 4. Starts an internal kickoff HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8082. 5. Writes status=waiting-kickoff. 6. Starts a background worker thread that waits for kickoff requests. 7. Keeps nginx in the foreground process group. --- ## Backend Startup MapServerKickoffService sends a kickoff only when: - mtl.map-server.tile-mode is local - a tile upstream URL is configured - the resolver can reach a healthy local sidecar The application-managed local map scope is always prod, including demo mode. Demo deployments therefore do not require a separate preloaded or area-limited map archive. If no local sidecar is healthy, the backend uses the hosted PMTiles upstream without logging a failed kickoff. --- ## Background Worker The worker receives a scope from /kickoff/{scope} and operates on: For normal app use, the scope is prod. ### Step A - Already ready The worker checks whether planet.pmtiles points to a real versioned file with a matching .done sentinel. If ready, it: - checks file permissions - ensures the low-zoom archive exists - refreshes symlinks - writes status=ready ### Step B - Incomplete download If a YYYYMMDD.pmtiles file exists without a .done sentinel, the worker resumes that exact version using the stored .url sentinel or reconstructs the Protomaps URL from the date. ### Step C - New runtime preparation If no ready or incomplete archive exists and MAP_DOWNLOAD_URL is configured, the worker resolves the URL, derives the build date, and prepares the archive. MAP_DOWNLOAD_URL=latest probes recent Protomaps daily builds through PROTOMAPS_BUILDS_BASE_URL, defaulting to https://build.protomaps.com. ### Step D - Nothing to serve If there is no archive and no MAP_DOWNLOAD_URL, the worker writes an error status. The Java backend can still use hosted PMTiles when the local sidecar is not selected. --- ## Download Modes ### Full planet mode When MAP_AREA_BBOX is empty: - wget --continue downloads the full PMTiles archive - progress is written to /tmp/map-status.json - YYYYMMDD.pmtiles.done is written on success - low-zoom extraction starts after the full archive is available ### Area-only mode When MAP_AREA_BBOX is set: - pmtiles extract <url> YYYYMMDD.pmtiles --bbox=... --maxzoom=15 - CDN range requests fetch only the requested area - low-zoom extraction can read from the remote source URL This mode remains available for custom local deployments, but it is no longer used for demo preloaded maps. --- ## Tile Serving The browser receives archive URLs like: or, when the local sidecar is healthy: MapTileProxyController: - validates scope and filename - rejects stale mtl-map-source / mtl-map-archive cache identities - appends private mtl-version (app container release), optional mtl-build (image build time), and mtl-server-id upstream; missing image metadata falls back to Maven metadata - forwards the resolved client IP in X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP headers - streams HTTP Range responses back to the browser nginx rejects PMTiles requests without mtl-version and mtl-server-id. The image build parameter is optional. ### Browser recovery The main map and mini-maps keep vector tiles after an individual tile error. They check a fresh PMTiles header and root directory before changing the basemap. Three failed checks, spaced by one and three seconds, enable temporary raster fallback. Each check has a five-second timeout. A healthy archive triggers a bounded tile or source retry; persistent tile errors do not cause a reload loop. Temporary raster checks the archive every 30 seconds and restores vector when available. Renderer disposal cancels pending checks. A failed main-map status probe also leaves vector enabled; an explicit download state still uses raster until preparation completes. --- ## Volume Layout Old versions are not auto-deleted to avoid accidental data loss. --- ## Environment Variables | Variable | Required | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | MAP_DOWNLOAD_URL | No | empty | latest to auto-resolve the most recent Protomaps build, or a direct URL. If empty, the orchestrator serves only existing tiles. | | PROTOMAPS_BUILDS_BASE_URL | No | https://build.protomaps.com | Daily-build base URL used when MAP_DOWNLOAD_URL=latest. | | MAP_AREA_BBOX | No | empty | west,south,east,north for area-only local extraction instead of full planet download. | | LOWZOOM_MAXZOOM | No | 6 | Maximum zoom level for the offline low-zoom extract. | | PORT | No | 8081 | nginx listen port. | --- ## Internal Kickoff API | Method | Path | Effect | |---|---|---| | PUT | /kickoff/prod | Checks existing tiles, resumes incomplete work, or starts runtime preparation. | | DELETE | /kickoff/prod | Removes symlinks, sentinels, and tile files in /data/prod, then reprocesses. | PUT and POST are both accepted.

title: Media architecture
text: # Media architecture - Media indexing - Media correlation - Media filtering - Media delivery

title: Media correlation
text: # Media correlation MTL Explorer places indexed photos and videos in activity context without changing their source metadata. Track Details includes a Media tab with a persisted timeline, position provenance, camera-clock correction, manual location assignment, and the shared media viewer. ## Position evidence and resolution Each source is stored separately so later information does not overwrite earlier evidence: - media_file.exif_gps_location keeps the embedded EXIF point unchanged. - media_track_correlation keeps every eligible activity correlation and its interpolated route point. - media_manual_location keeps the point and note entered by the user. - media_resolved_location is the small indexed projection used by map reads. The resolved position uses this precedence: 1. USER_ASSIGNED 2. EXIF_EMBEDDED 3. TRACK_INTERPOLATED Timeline and trend-item responses carry positionOrigin, shown as Set by you , Photo GPS , or Estimated . Clearing a user assignment exposes the preserved EXIF or track-derived position again. A track-derived position never creates EXIF GPS metadata. If provenance is unavailable, the client shows Position unknown instead of assuming embedded GPS. ## Capture time and activity matching EXIF GPS time is authoritative when present. Otherwise, EXIF DateTimeOriginal is used with an optional saved camera offset from -24 to +24 hours. Corrections are stored separately in media_time_correction and never modify source timestamps. Only successful, unique, imported activities with supported recorded timing and timestamped canonical points are eligible. Estimated or unsupported timing cannot supply time-based matches. Map/statistics use decisions do not erase an otherwise supported correlation; selection still controls map and trend scope. All overlapping activity correlations are retained. The selected match is deterministic: a photo with GPS prefers the nearest route; remaining ties use interval midpoint, duration, then activity id. The response includes ambiguousMatch and alternativeMatchCount when more than one activity was eligible. Map-point responses contain coordinates only; the ordinary media-details response does not carry this provenance. A viewer needs the collection item's provenance to label its position. Track position is interpolated between the canonical points around the adjusted capture time. The stored correlation includes route position, distance, duration, nearest point index and time delta, algorithm version, activity version, applied offset, and calculation time. ## Incremental correlation job Correlation is asynchronous and durable. Media metadata changes, saved time or manual-location changes, activity changes, and authoritative RAW_OUTLIER_CLEANED track-data changes add small work items. Track work first expands to media in the activity's old or new indexed time window. Media work is then processed in bounded batches. A failed batch is retried one item at a time. Deterministic failures are deferred with an error summary so later work continues instead of repeatedly blocking the queue. This avoids comparing every photo with every activity. Replacing or deleting an activity also requeues its previously correlated photos so they can fall back to another match, EXIF, or no resolved position. An algorithm-version marker allows stale rows to be recalculated after the matching rules change. Reads keep the last completed result while recalculation is pending. Admin job status reports the remaining correlation work. Normal read paths do no interpolation: - map bounds query the GiST-indexed media_resolved_location projection; - an activity timeline queries a bounded page through the (track_id, adjusted_capture_time, media_id) selected-correlation index; - the original media content remains loaded only when a thumbnail or viewer requests it. ## API The OpenAPI schema is the source of truth and the frontend uses its generated TypeScript client. - GET /mtl/api/media/by-track/{trackId} returns a page envelope when cameraOffsetSeconds=0; a non-zero offset returns the corresponding unsaved preview page. page is zero-based, pageSize defaults to 100 and is limited to 200, and the response includes total item and page counts. - POST /mtl/api/media/trends returns grouped photo/video counts within the matching tracks' continuous time range. Track related also requires a selected correlation to a matching track. See selection semantics . - POST /mtl/api/media/trends/items returns a stable newest-first page for one trend period and optional photo/video kind filter. The UI requests 60 items per page. - PUT /mtl/api/media/time-corrections saves or clears reversible corrections for a bounded media-id set and returns 204 No Content. - PUT /mtl/api/media/{mediaId}/manual-location saves a user assignment. - DELETE /mtl/api/media/{mediaId}/manual-location clears it. A missing activity or media item returns 404. Invalid coordinates, offsets, or request sizes return 400. See the media guide for browsing and corrections.

title: Media delivery
text: # Media delivery The browser requests bounded previews and original content separately from metadata. Server content reads preserve source freshness, cache identity, and HTTP Range support for video. Image previews use libvips first and a logged ImageMagick fallback when the native loader cannot decode a format. Video posters and optional H.264/AAC HLS conversion use server-side media tools. Conversion work is bounded and cancellable; the original remains available. Map collections and activity timelines load pages. The filmstrip retains a bounded thumbnail window and fetches another page at navigation boundaries. The viewer owns display state; it does not calculate activity associations. Thumbnail buttons preserve native lazy loading and browser caching. After a native load error, they recover through the same image fetch helper as viewer previews. The helper allows one preview and one thumbnail request at a time, including response-body reading. A running thumbnail does not block a cached preview. Queued thumbnails wait until all previews finish, including HTTP 503 retry waits, so they do not compete for the server's converter between preview attempts. Each admitted request has a 90-second timeout covering headers and body transfer. Queue time does not consume that timeout or the retry budget. Thumbnails allow 30 busy retries; previews allow 90, enough to outlast a thumbnail conversion. Retry delays are between one and two seconds. A retry releases its request slot so another preview can proceed. Abort removes queued work and releases active requests on navigation. Thumbnail removal, source changes, and hiding grids while a viewer is open cancel recovery and revoke recovered blob URLs. Exhausted or undecodable thumbnails show “No preview”. Their button still opens media and also restarts thumbnail recovery unless the click was prevented. Filmstrip drag suppression prevents both selection and recovery. The media build notes define packaged dependencies and regression checks. See video playback for the user flow.

title: Media filtering
text: # Media filtering The filter result defines the media time range in MTL Explorer. 1. Resolve the actual matching track IDs, including for custom filters. 2. On the server, take the earliest valid start and latest valid end of those tracks. 3. Include media whose capture time falls within that continuous interval, including both endpoints. Filter names, date fields, weeks, activity categories and SQL parameters are never interpreted to infer a second time filter. Track visibility and map colors do not alter the result. Tracks without a finite, complete start/end interval, or with an end before their start, cannot define the range. No matching dated tracks means no media. For example, if matching tracks run from September 5 at 09:00 through September 17 at 18:00, that is the media interval. A photo on September 10 is included even if no track exists that day. A photo on September 4 is excluded. Selecting a nominal two-week period can therefore yield a narrower media interval, depending on the actual matching tracks.
