Remove the browser findings-token comparison and processingFindingsAcknowledged storage. Remove the unused freshness snooze, dismiss handler, storage key, and obsolete snooze tests. Retain freshness detection, reload behaviour, and their tests. 3. Verify the complete lifecycle and demo flow. Update processing, GPS review, media, map, and architecture documentation when the behaviour is implemented. Regenerate the website and installed guide from their sources. ### Acceptance checks - Per-file and bulk acknowledgement produce the same saved result. Neither changes use settings, source contents, or metric support. - The overall action on the map and Settings → Processing covers all pending GPS/media source issues in its snapshot, including files beyond the visible list page. Group actions cover only their index. - Each mass action sends one full target array in one write request, with no per-file or pagination submission loop. Server writes use set-based SQL or bounded internal batches, rather than per-issue repository calls. - After a successful save, Processing clears acknowledged source attention, and map/Review counts agree with it. Failed/skipped totals remain factual, running work retains its progress, and correlated unavailable calculations do not demand another acceptance of the same source limitation. - A failed bulk transaction clears no warning and commits no acknowledgement. Changed or newly arriving issues remain pending; returned counts show the actual result, including stale targets. - The same account stays quiet after normal logout, clearing browser data, later login, another device, and server restart. Other accounts remain independent. - Unchanged retries and rescans, cosmetic diagnosis changes, and removal of other issues do not restore acknowledged notices. - Changed contents or a new semantic defect require review even when the total issue count is unchanged. Remaining acknowledged defects stay quiet. - Issues arriving during bulk acknowledgement and stale per-file requests cannot be silently acknowledged. Duplicate inserts keep one acknowledgement row and its original timestamp; repeating Reopen leaves it absent. - Reopen affects only the current account. Concurrent opposite actions follow database write ordering, with no stronger replay guarantee. Login case variants share the canonical account key; login/session references do not determine acknowledgement ownership. - Demo visitors using the configured login share acknowledgements. Resetting demo data clears its acknowledgements without affecting another installation. - Incomplete assessments do not resolve findings they could not check. Source removal retains resolved issue history; explicit database deletion removes dependent rows consistently. - Corrected or removed sources resolve their corresponding issues. Imported GPS quality findings remain pending until acknowledged or actually resolved. - Stable zero-byte GPS and media files appear as informational skips without a map review notice. Changed contents are processed again. Damaged and unsupported contents remain reviewable. - Pending counts agree across the map, Review, and other review summaries and count each source file once. Technical outcome totals remain accurate. - Normalized severity preserves the existing GPS review policy, including the assessment-limit exception. A domain severity escalation changes its finding identity even if normalized severity remains REVIEW. - Processing, freshness, offline, and service-failure indicators remain accurate independently of source acknowledgement. Use public or synthetic fixtures. Run backend checks in the development container and relevant client tests for these contracts.

title: JFR Profiling
text: # JFR Profiling The runtime image includes jattach, not a full JDK. Replace <container> with the app container name. For container memory, use cgroup counters: The source image uses G1 with MaxRAMPercentage=40.0 and InitialRAMPercentage=6.25. At the default 1248 MiB app container limit, Java 25 G1 rounds the maximum heap to 500 MiB and the initial heap to 78 MiB. A 1176 MiB limit gives a 472 MiB maximum heap and a 74 MiB initial heap. Demo preparation finishes before Java starts. The remaining 60% of the app limit covers JVM native allocations and the shared media process slot, which allows one libvips, ImageMagick, FFprobe or FFmpeg child at a time by default. Heap capacity is only part of the JVM's total memory usage. A synthetic 4K HEVC to 1080p HLS conversion used about 328 MiB of FFmpeg RSS; a 256 MiB helper container failed, while 384 MiB completed. Historical JVM native allocations were about 300 MiB. These separate measurements guide the budget; they do not establish a safe combined limit for every workload. A focused ARM64 check ran synthetic GPX imports and 1080p conversion together under the default app limit. Larger workloads and AMD64 memory peaks remain unverified. Larger media or more concurrent helpers may require a larger app limit. Upgrade to an image containing this profile to apply the new percentage. Raising both Compose memory and swap limits and recreating the app container scales the heap according to the running image's percentage. Other limits or JVM options may change the effective heap; check it with GC.heap_info above. Remove any fixed -Xmx override from JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS, or a custom Java command when adopting automatic heap sizing. Keep unrelated JVM options. A fixed heap size takes precedence over the percentage. See container memory limits for the Compose settings. The published 0.8.1 Dockerfile used ZGC with MaxRAMPercentage=50.0. ZGC process RSS could count multiple mappings of the same heap pages. Use cgroup usage and OOM events for container decisions, and inspect the running image's JVM arguments before comparing profiles. ## Container memory limits The default Compose file uses these settings. Memory and swap limits are equal, which disables container swap. | Service | Memory and swap limit | Related settings | | --- | --- | --- | | app | 1248 MiB | Image heap profile: 40%; routing timeout: MTL_PLANNER_BROUTER_TIMEOUT_MS=310000 | | db | 512 MiB | Keep the complete PostgreSQL command, including shared_buffers=64MB, work_mem=1MB, and max_connections=20 | | brouter | 512 MiB | BROUTER_JAVA_XMX=128m | | location-search | 128 MiB | MTL_LOCATION_SEARCH_MMAP_SIZE=33554432 (32 MiB) | | map-server (optional) | 128 MiB | LOWZOOM_MAXZOOM=6 | The limits are at least 20 percent above historical validated limits: 640 MiB for the standard app, 384 MiB for PostgreSQL and BRouter, and 96 MiB for location search and maps. Those checks used earlier app workloads and heap settings; they do not establish a 20 percent margin for the current app with 1080p conversion. BRouter was checked with routes up to about 1,500 km. The map limit was checked while extracting its zoom 0-6 overview and serving concurrent range requests. Compose allows a routing request up to 310 seconds, just above BRouter's 300-second route ceiling. Large image or video conversions use the app headroom one at a time. Docker and the operating system need additional memory. When raising a limit, set the memory and swap limits to the same value, then recreate the container. A process restart does not apply changed limits or environment settings. Every installation uses a local Compose file, including copies held by NAS container managers. Compare it with the new release's template and merge the settings for every service you run. Keep your credentials, ports, mounts, and deliberately larger limits. Apply the related settings above together with their memory limits; copy the full PostgreSQL command from the template. For the current image, the default app limit needs no fixed heap override. Merge this example into the existing app service: Validate the edited Compose file with docker compose config --quiet, then recreate the affected services with docker compose up -d. With the current image, the default 1248 MiB limit, and no fixed heap override, the app startup log should report heapMaxMiB=500.0. Larger limits produce a larger heap; check the effective size with GC.heap_info.

title: Release updates
text: # Release updates Starting with 0.9.0, MTL Explorer checks a small public JSON feed at https://mtl-explorer.com/releases/releases.json. The server performs the check; browsers only request the cached result from /mtl/api/info/updates. ## User flow - One notice introduces an available release. Dismiss keeps the Settings badge. - Desktop Settings and mobile More show the shared glowing dot. Expanded mobile Settings keeps the Update label. - View update or Settings → Updates opens versions, the summary, release notes, and update instructions. - Skip this version hides its notice and badge. The next release can notify again. - Reminder preferences belong to the browser, signed-in username, and installation. - The installation owner updates Docker Compose. Detection never installs or restarts anything. - After a detected installation change, one completion notice links to the notes. - A waiting browser service worker offers Reload or Later , including before login. Release offers remain signed-in only. Later keeps the navigation dot, a Reload label in expanded mobile Settings, and a reload action in Updates; it never interrupts work automatically. ## Identities | Identity | Example | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | Public release | 0.9.0 | Display, release notes, semantic version comparison | | Immutable image build | 1.520 | Match the running Docker image to the public catalog | | Image digest | sha256:… | Verify the exact published image before offering it | | Git revision | commit SHA | Private build traceability and diagnostics | Images carry their immutable build identity; public versions are chosen when publishing and bound to verified builds in the release catalog. No public version is bundled in the application. Docker build tags keep their existing numbering; Git history does not decide release order. The public feed contains no private Git revision, tree, or build record. About shows the image build and, when the cached catalog identifies the installed component combination, its deployment release. Before a feed is available, the semantic release remains unknown. Local frontend builds show their development package version. Retain published mappings so older installations remain identifiable. The feed maps releases to immutable builds and has separate channel pointers. The same build promoted to a public release is already installed. An unregistered custom or older build reports unknown rather than guessing. Earlier versions do not acquire this checker retroactively: 0.9.0 is the first checking installation, and its first normal offer will be a later release. Preview screenshots use an isolated synthetic 0.8.1 → 0.9.0 mapping to illustrate the flow. ## Components and deployment releases One notice and badge cover self-managed MTL components. Updates lists the server, routing, location search, and maps with installed and target image builds. Provider-managed services are informational; disabled services are ignored. Unknown ownership or builds never imply an update or incompatibility. Unknown ownership stays visible on the component row but does not block the overall status or completion notice for tracked, self-managed components. An unknown build in a self-managed component still prevents claiming it is current. The feed's optional components map describes a tested deployment combination. Each target contains buildId, image, and digest. Component IDs are app, brouter, location-search, and map-server. The existing top-level image fields must match components.app. Feeds without a component map retain application-only behavior. Public release versions describe the combination; individual image build tags remain independent. Git revisions are diagnostic only. A component-only release may reuse the application image. Installed release identity comes from the self-managed component combination; the completion notice uses its component inventory, so updating search alone clears its offer. Registered builds from later releases are never offered a downgrade. Custom unregistered builds remain unknown. Each component build identity has one immutable image/digest binding across all releases. Optional compatibleBuildIds lists explicitly supported older builds; the target build is always supported. Omit the list when compatibility is unconfirmed. An explicit list excluding a known older build marks that component as requiring an update for the target release. This does not affect application health or disable features. Provider API rollouts must preserve compatibility with supported clients; release discovery is not a service-health check. Ownership is configured, never guessed from a URL. A remote service can still be self-managed. Compose defaults routing/search to SELF_MANAGED and maps to PROVIDER_MANAGED. For provider-managed routing/search, change the corresponding environment values. For local maps, enable local-maps and set MTL_UPDATES_MAP_SERVER_MANAGEMENT=SELF_MANAGED. | Compose environment variable | Default | | --- | --- | | MTL_UPDATES_BROUTER_MANAGEMENT | SELF_MANAGED | | MTL_UPDATES_LOCATION_SEARCH_MANAGEMENT | SELF_MANAGED | | MTL_UPDATES_MAP_SERVER_MANAGEMENT | PROVIDER_MANAGED | Allowed values: SELF_MANAGED, PROVIDER_MANAGED, DISABLED, UNKNOWN. Outside Compose, ownership defaults to UNKNOWN. Spring configuration uses mtl.updates.components.<component-id>.management and optional .status-url; otherwise existing component status URLs are used. Environment property names remove component hyphens, for example MTL_UPDATES_COMPONENTS_LOCATIONSEARCH_MANAGEMENT. Self-managed maps require a reachable status URL: enable local-maps for the Compose service, or configure mtl.updates.components.map-server.status-url for a remote service. An unavailable map service affects its own observation; other components continue checking. Use PROVIDER_MANAGED or DISABLED when that matches the installation; ownership is never inferred from reachability. Only self-managed, enabled services are probed. Their status response supplies versionInfo.image.version. Requests run in the update worker with a 3-second whole-request deadline and the same size limit as the feed. Provider-managed and unknown services receive no update-discovery requests. Snapshots never wait for network activity. Successful observations refresh on demand at most once per minute; failures retain the last build and back off for 15 minutes. Manual checks can retry after one minute. The browser allows the feed plus three sequential component probes to finish within its 35-second request deadline. PostgreSQL/PostGIS maintenance remains an operator task, with separate major upgrade instructions. Embedded libraries belong to their image release. Map and routing dataset freshness remains separate from software updates. The checker never reads the Docker socket, installs images, or restarts services. ## Network restrictions Checks run in a separate background worker and never block startup, normal API requests, imports, or navigation. Connection timeout is 3 seconds; the whole request, including a stalled body, is bounded to 12 seconds and 256 KiB. Refused connections, DNS/TLS errors, HTTP failures, invalid feeds, and component probe failures produce a short INFO log; stack traces are DEBUG only. There is no global warning, error dialog, or failed health status. Updates shows a quiet explanation. The last valid result stays cached in memory if a refresh fails. Unknown component IDs and channels are ignored. Invalid releases and their channel pointers are skipped; conflicting build bindings exclude every affected release. Broken feed structure or unsupported schemas still reject the response. Additive changes must retain schemaVersion: 1. A breaking schema needs a new endpoint while the existing URL continues serving schema 1 for older installations. Publication dates are validated by the publisher, independently of the consuming server's date and time zone. An active browser checks the cached API hourly and on focus/reconnection. The server fetches at most daily, with a 15-minute failure retry gate and a one-minute manual-check gate. Concurrent browsers share the server result. No installed identity, username, or archive data is sent to the feed. To make no release-feed requests, set MTL_UPDATES_ENABLED=false in the Compose environment and recreate the app container. MTL_UPDATES_CHANNEL defaults to stable; align it with the image channel you run. Development checks are disabled by default, as are demo checks. Offline installations can update manually. For a private mirror or test feed, set MTL_UPDATES_FEED_URL in the Compose environment or .env, then recreate the app container: The default remains https://mtl-explorer.com/releases/releases.json. The URL must serve the same release-feed JSON over HTTP or HTTPS and be reachable from the server container. For a test server on the Mac host, use http://host.docker.internal:18769/releases/releases.json; container localhost refers to the container itself. Outside Compose, set Spring's mtl.updates.feed-url or the environment variable MTL_UPDATES_FEEDURL. Compose maps the readable MTL_UPDATES_FEED_URL name to this Spring environment name. The browser continues to use the server's cached result. ## Release publication 1. Choose the public version and prepare its reviewed release notes. Keep released_on: null until publication. 2. Commit the application source and build an unused immutable Docker tag with docker-build-deploy.py, or select an existing verified build. Build records identify the image by build ID and digest, independently of the public version. 3. Publish/promote the image channel intended for users and verify it. Keep the generated image record in the private repository; never invent a digest or reuse a published build tag. For stable, promote the tested build to Docker latest: Replace BUILD with the unused tag you actually built. The record is in ../mtl-explorer-private/docs-my/operations/releases/builds/mytraillog-BUILD.json by default. Commit it in the private repository. See container builds for output overrides. 4. Set the note's actual publication date. Run the normal publisher with the record, for example: 5. The publisher checks the immutable image and the corresponding Docker channel (stable → latest) against the record's live registry digest before binding the release in documentation/release-notes/artifacts.json. It regenerates the homepage, notes, archive, and docs/releases/releases.json before copying the mirror. Commit the reviewed source catalog and generated output in the primary repo. 6. Publish through the existing confirmations, then check the public feed, notes, update guide, and a registered older installation. Published bindings are immutable. Draft notes, unregistered notes, sync-only, release-only, and GitHub draft/prerelease operations do not create update offers. The public catalog starts empty; no historical image mappings are inferred. The current website tooling uses numeric public release versions. Beta/alpha pointers can select published numeric releases; prerelease note authoring is outside this first implementation. For example, --update-channel beta verifies Docker :beta and advances the beta feed pointer for v.0.9.0. It does not require GitHub's --prerelease flag; that flag intentionally excludes publication from the update feed. Numeric beta/alpha releases appear in the website's regular release list. When creating their GitHub release, the publisher also explicitly passes --latest; the update channel does not isolate them from public release announcements. ## Isolated E2E preview Use an existing development container for Java and a disposable database. Never change production channels or the real public catalog to simulate an update. Set the test server's MTL_IMAGE_VERSION=1.508, enable checks, and point MTL_UPDATES_FEED_URL (Compose) or mtl.updates.feed-url (Spring) to the fixture URL reachable from its container. Verify notice, dismissal/reload, badge, details, skip, and restore on desktop and phone. Restart only that test server with build 1.520: the badge clears and one completion notice appears. Point it to a refused or stalled endpoint and verify login, map interaction, normal API calls, INFO logging, and Updates fallback. For a browser-worker upgrade, serve two distinct production frontend builds at one test origin: wait for Reload, choose Later, confirm work is retained, then reload explicitly. A development Vite server does not register that worker. Automated coverage: ReleaseFeedClientTest, ReleaseUpdateServiceTest, ReleaseComponentInventoryTest, releaseUpdatesStore.spec.ts, releaseUpdateDetails.spec.ts, test_release_feed.py, and test_release_publication.py. See application verification and component verification . ## Publishing a component bundle Full Docker builds also write mtl-bundle-BUILD.json, named for the application build ID, in the same private release-record directory. App-only builds record only the app. Commit the manifest in the private repository before publication. Use --bundle-record PATH instead of --image-record PATH with ../mtl-explorer-private/publish-to-github.py, for example: The publisher verifies every listed immutable image digest and selected Docker channel before registering the bundle. It never installs it. For a component-only release, explicitly select the previous tested bundle and replace the changed artifact with its published immutable image: Replace BUILD with the actual immutable tag. The helper reads its registry digest and retains unchanged components. Repeat --component for more changes; use --component app=IMAGE:BUILD to retain sidecars after an app-only build. If the base record contains only the app, explicitly add each sidecar to track with another --component argument. Changed artifacts do not inherit old compatibility claims. The helper neither promotes channels nor publishes, and refuses to overwrite an existing record. Test the resulting combination, promote its selected channels, and pass the record to ../mtl-explorer-private/publish-to-github.py --bundle-record with the chosen public version. App-only build records remain app-only unless a base is explicitly selected. Every bundle includes the unchanged application artifact. Existing component build tags cannot be overwritten; full builds reject reused tags for every image they build. Tag-only mode promotes existing artifacts. Keep private Git metadata out of the manifest. For reproducible deployments, pin Compose overrides to the verified manifest digests. Independent moving latest tags do not establish compatibility. Update only affected services according to release notes; database major upgrades have a separate operator procedure. To preview a component-only offer with an unchanged server image, add --components to documentation.tools.website.prepare_update_preview. The synthetic catalog offers 0.9.1 to server build 1.508 and search build 2.1; search 2.2 clears it.

title: Frontend styling
text: # Frontend styling PrimeVue uses the Lara preset customized in setupPrimeVue.ts . Its dark-mode selector follows the app’s data-theme attribute. Shared colors, typography, and layer tokens live in base.css ; shared classes live in main.css . ## PrimeVue components Prefer the component’s design tokens for colors, dimensions, and spacing. Inspect the installed @primeuix/themes preset and @primeuix/styles component CSS before choosing a token. Token names become --p- CSS variables, such as button.padding.x → --p-button-padding-x. Overriding only a rendered handle’s width can leave token-based centering calculations unchanged. Change the related tokens together when resizing a PrimeVue control. Use scoped :deep() rules for integration or layout that has no suitable token; verify the actual rendered component. ## Shared app controls Use MtlSlider for the app’s single-value, range, and opacity sliders. It owns pointer and keyboard handling, ARIA values, track layout, and touch targets. PrimeVue Slider tokens do not resize this component. Use BottomSheet for mobile tools, editors, and content panels. Keep panel sizing, dragging, scrolling, and close controls in that shared component. Panels overlay the map without changing map-control, attribution, or toolbar offsets. Use the existing SectionHub, settings rows, and typography roles for new flows. Keep entry-hub introductions subdued and informational, using the standard heading and body typography. Put primary navigation in the rows below; keep introductory links small and contextual. Do not add eyebrow labels or separate caption styles. Place reusable styling at the shared owner; keep topic-specific layout in its component. Transient messages and persistent update prompts share AppNotifications and NotificationCard . Send messages through the toast service; use warn for warnings. Update prompts provide actions and stay visible until the user acts. Keep one toast host so messages stack without overlapping. ## Verification Check the complete flow in both themes and at desktop and phone widths. Verify keyboard focus, touch targets, long text, disabled states, and local scrolling for tables or code. Use pointer: coarse when a change specifically concerns touch input. Keep JavaScript and CSS layer ordering consistent. Run relevant frontend checks from the frontend workflow .

title: Testing
text: # Testing Choose checks for the changed behavior. Keep reusable instructions here; dated outcomes belong in internal verification. - Unit and integration checks - Google Health import simulation - End-user and indexer regression - Indexer regression cases - Security checks - Documentation checks For repeatable end-user checks: - Full-regression workflow and coverage - GPS regression - Media regression and video playback - Quick installation and container build Use public or fully synthetic data. Never derive fixtures from private GPX tracks. Java checks run in the existing development container. Preserve pre-existing failures separately from results for the change.

title: Full regression
text: # Full regression Use this workflow for a complete end-user run with frozen coverage and resumable packets. 1. Read the workflow . 2. Review the coverage plan . 3. Start a run with the goal prompt . 4. Record packets and check the finalization gate. Dated run evidence is stored internally. New coverage applies to new runs; existing runs retain their own snapshots.

title: Regression Test Plan
text: # Regression Test Plan Manual checklist for validating MTL Explorer end-to-end. Most checks use the app UI. Fixture setup, service-state changes, and API evidence need access to the disposable test environment. For each item, perform the action and confirm the expected result. Note any deviation, including blank screens, error toasts, slow responses, or visually broken layouts. Fresh-server runs do not use a personal Google account. They check Google Health disabled, unconfigured, empty, and demo states only. Connected Health checks are a separate local pass with the owner's existing account; see Google Health scope . Do not copy account credentials, tokens, local health data, or private tracks to a test server or report assets. ## Coverage Accounting Coverage IDs such as TRD_01 are stable report references. Once added, an ID must never be renamed, renumbered, reused, or changed to mean a different check. Add new checks with the next unused number in the closest matching ID prefix. If a check becomes obsolete, keep the ID and mark it NOT APPLICABLE or explain the replacement. Packet results and full-regression reports must reference coverage IDs, not section numbers alone. | Prefix | Area | |---|---| | ACC | Coverage accounting | | DAT, IMP, DEL, FIT, FMT | Required data-change flows | | SGN | Sign-in and first load | | MAP | Map and tracks | | TRD | Track details | | FLT | Filters | | TBS | Track browser and statistics | | PLN | Planner | | MCT | Measuring and comparison tools | | AVR | Animation and virtual race | | MED | Media | | HMO | Heatmap and overlays | | GPS | GPS location | | SRC | Location search | | GLB | Globe mode | | ADM | Settings and operations | | SYN | Data updates and sync | | GHL | Google Health optionality and local connected checks | | APP | Appearance | | LOC | Locale, units, and formatting | | MOB | Responsive mobile and touch | | NET | Offline and network issues | | ERR | Error recovery | | UXP | UX performance | - ACC_01 Treat every checklist bullet as a required coverage item unless it is explicitly not applicable to the run. - ACC_02 Do not mark a section PASS when any bullet inside it was skipped, only spot-checked, or verified indirectly. Mark the section PARTIAL, NOT COVERED, NOT APPLICABLE, BLOCKED, or FAIL as appropriate. - ACC_03 In full-regression reports, include enough coverage detail to show which bullets were actually exercised and which were not. Broad section summaries are acceptable only when all child bullets have supporting evidence. - ACC_04 Capture compact screenshots for representative working user-facing functions as well as failures, so reports provide a visual overview and not only defect evidence. - ACC_05 If time, tooling, viewport, data, permissions, or environment constraints prevent a check, record that constraint explicitly instead of silently collapsing the check into a parent row. ## Required Data-Change Regression Run this in every full regression and every release-candidate data-change pass. ### Public Test Data - DAT_01 Use at least five public internet GPX files with real track sequences (trk / trkseg / trkpt). Waypoint-only files (wpt without trkpt) are not valid positive import evidence. - DAT_02 Prefer GPX files with timestamped trackpoints so duration, speed, moving time, and period statistics can be verified. - DAT_03 Record for every source file: source URL, source page/license note, destination filename, SHA-256, byte size, trkpt count, timestamp count, imported track id(s), and imported track name(s). - DAT_04 Suggested verified GPX source: https://github.com/gps-touring/sample-gpx with raw files such as: - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gps-touring/sample-gpx/master/BrittanyJura/JuraRoute72011.gpx - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gps-touring/sample-gpx/master/BrittanyJura/MoselradwegAusWiki.gpx - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gps-touring/sample-gpx/master/BrittanyJura/Vitry-le-Francois_Langres.gpx - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gps-touring/sample-gpx/master/BrittanyJura/VoieVerteHauteVosges.gpx - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gps-touring/sample-gpx/master/RoscoffCoastal/Lannion_Plestin_parcours24.4RE.gpx - DAT_05 Use at least one public FIT activity file with GPS positions . Suggested verified FIT source: Garmin's official FIT SDK examples, e.g. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garmin/fit-javascript-sdk/main/test/data/Activity.fit. - DAT_06 Do not count non-GPS FIT files or waypoint-only GPX files as positive evidence. They are useful negative tests only: MTL Explorer should fail, ignore, or mark them clearly without adding map tracks, corrupting stats, or blanking the UI. - DAT_07 For measure / comparison / virtual-race checks, include at least one repeatable two-point segment with two or more tracks crossing the same two zones. Use public tracks or fully synthetic anonymized GPX data; do not use private local GPX files as fixtures or report evidence. - DAT_08 Use the fully synthetic, non-private media set generated by the packaged /app/demo/generate_regression_photos.py helper. It uses the same shared renderer as the demo photos and ffmpeg for short videos. The helper produces four GPS JPEGs, two camera-time-only JPEGs, one H.264/AAC MP4 with embedded GPS and capture time, one H.264/AAC MOV with capture time but no GPS, and a matching six-point synthetic GPX activity. Record the generated manifest, including checksums and ffprobe data. Copy the GPX into data/gpx/<run-id>/ and all eight media files into data/media/<run-id>/; keep the manifest and deletion backups outside the watched media tree. - DAT_09 Prepare fully synthetic GPS cases for timing and motion: repeated visits to two ordered zones, a recorded pause below one minute, a longer observed stop, a source recording break, and missing/repeated/reversed timestamps. Record expected intervals and geometry independently of displayed results. Keep these fixtures outside the five-GPX count assertions and retain them through segment/replay checks. Do not derive them from local tracks. ### Five-GPX Import, Index, Map, And Stats Flow - IMP_01 Capture baseline map count, track-browser count, statistics totals, data-freshness token, and GPS indexer status. - IMP_02 Import the five GPX files through the Settings → Import & sync upload UI or by placing them in the documented watched import folder. - IMP_03 Wait for indexing to finish. If live file watching does not react, trigger Rescan GPS from Settings → Maintenance and record that it was needed. - IMP_04 Confirm upload/index status: all five source files reach completed state, no unexpected GPS index failures appear, data freshness changes, and background jobs (Duplicate Finder, Exploration Score) settle. - IMP_05 Reload from the freshness banner or helper reload action → the map, track browser, filters, and statistics all show the new data. - IMP_06 Verify each imported file by name: it appears in track browser search, on the map, in statistics summaries, and in at least one filter result. - IMP_07 On the map, zoom to the imported tracks, click each track, verify selection/detail opening, point popups, visible line geometry, and no stale or duplicated lines. - IMP_08 In statistics, verify count increased by five unless a source file legitimately split into multiple tracks; if it split, record the source-to-track mapping and expected count. - IMP_09 Verify totals changed in the correct direction: total distance, duration, ascent/descent, activity breakdown, period charts, rankings, heatmap density, and track-browser summary row. ### Delete-Two-Track Flow - DEL_01 Delete two of the imported source files from the watched import/upload folder. If the test environment only exposes browser upload and not the watched folder, mark deletion sync BLOCKED and run this flow in the install/full-regression environment. - DEL_02 Wait for automatic delete processing or trigger Rescan GPS . - DEL_03 Verify the two deleted tracks disappear from the map, track browser, filter results, selection lists, heatmap, related-track lists, and statistics totals. - DEL_04 Verify the remaining imported tracks still display and open correctly. - DEL_05 Deleted-track API probes or stale deleted-track URLs are not pass/fail criteria for this deletion flow. The frontend regression requirement is that deleted tracks no longer appear in user-visible map, browser, filter, heatmap, related-track, detail, or statistics surfaces. ### FIT Conversion Flow - FIT_01 Import the FIT activity file with GPS positions. - FIT_02 Verify it is accepted by upload/import, indexed successfully, displayed on the map, searchable in the browser, and included in statistics. - FIT_03 Open the FIT-backed track details → overview, graphs, quality, events, related tracks, mini-map, and point popups render as they do for GPX-backed tracks. - FIT_04 Download original source file → the downloaded file remains FIT and matches the uploaded checksum. - FIT_05 Download as GPX → a valid GPX file downloads and contains real trkpt trackpoints, not only waypoints. - FIT_06 If GPSBabel or FIT conversion is unavailable, the UI shows a clear conversion/indexing error and the failure is recorded as blocking for FIT support. ### Other Supported Track Formats - FMT_01 The server accepts .gpx, .fit, .tcx, .kml, .kmz, .igc, .nmea, .geojson, and .gdb. For a full release regression, test at least one GPS-bearing sample for each available format, or mark that format NOT COVERED with the reason. - FMT_02 For each non-GPX format tested, verify upload acceptance, GPSBabel conversion, map display, details/charts, statistics inclusion, Download original source file , and Download as GPX . ### Media Fixture Setup Flow - MED_06 Capture the media count, MEDIA indexer status, and media freshness baseline. Import the DAT_08 matching GPX first and wait for GPS indexing. Place all six generated JPEGs and both generated videos in the watched media folder, open Settings → Maintenance, trigger Rescan Media , and wait for MEDIA indexing and correlation to settle. Accept the freshness reload and verify all eight files are completed without failures. Preserve the generated manifest and exact source files outside the watched tree for later deletion evidence and recovery. ## 1. Sign-in And First Load - SGN_01 Open the app while signed out → you are redirected to the login screen. - SGN_02 Sign in with valid credentials → you reach the map. - SGN_03 Sign in with wrong credentials → a clear error appears and you stay on login. - SGN_04 If demo mode is active, the login screen shows the demo credentials banner. - SGN_05 Sign out → you return to login; signing in again works. - SGN_06 The splash screen (logo, background, message) displays during startup and disappears once the map and tracks are loaded. - SGN_07 If startup fails (e.g. server down), a retry is offered instead of a frozen splash. - SGN_08 "MTL Explorer" branding appears in About / public-facing copy. - SGN_09 Browser back/forward navigation between views works without errors. - SGN_10 On desktop and phone, in light and dark themes, Sign In retains its translucent background, blur, white label, and visible keyboard focus. Check hover where supported, original field height and blur, and demo banner readability; successful and failed sign-in retain the same treatment on return. ## 2. Map And Tracks - MAP_01 Base map and overlays load on first open. - MAP_02 All your tracks appear on the map; the total/visible count is correct. - MAP_03 Newly imported tracks from the required data-change flow appear without a full browser restart after accepting the freshness/reload prompt. - MAP_04 Deleted tracks from the required data-change flow disappear from all map sources, selection lists, and popups. - MAP_05 Zoom in on a track → detail/precision improves (no duplicate or broken lines). - MAP_06 Fast pan/zoom doesn't leave stale lines, missing tiles, or runaway loading spinners. - MAP_07 Direction arrows appear on tracks at high zoom when Track Points & Direction is enabled. Use a track whose current high-zoom rendered shape has visible in-viewport point vertices. A sparse two-point or straight synthetic track whose endpoints are outside the viewport is not valid evidence: the line may cross the screen while no arrow marker is expected at the visible midpoint. - MAP_08 Click a single track → it highlights and details open. - MAP_09 Click an area where several tracks overlap → a selection list appears; picking one opens its details. Categories whose lookups complete with no results have no chip or result group. Pending and failed/cancelled categories stay visible. If a selected pending category completes empty, All becomes active and shows the remaining results or “Nothing found here”. GPS details open expanded without widening the standard desktop panel. They use a separate foreground sheet; mobile details fill the screen to the top. The dispatcher keeps a constant height while details open, resize and close. Back, Close and browser Back reveal its unchanged size and category/page. - MAP_10 Deselect / close the selection → the map returns to its normal state. - MAP_11 Clicking a rendered track-point marker shows a popup with the expected metrics (time, speed, elevation, etc.). Click an actual direction-arrow/point marker, not only the connecting track line. - MAP_12 Swiss Mobility routes popup (where applicable) shows nearby official routes and closes cleanly. - MAP_13 Intentional remote raster mode: with mtl.map-server.tile-mode=remote, /api/map/config exposes remoteRasterStyles for light, light-topo, and dark, and does not expose legacy remoteTileUrl. Select OSM Light, OSM Topo Light, and OSM Dark; each loads map tiles from its configured provider URL, shows the matching attribution, keeps the map interactive, and makes no /api/map-proxy tile requests. - MAP_14 Remote raster fallback from local vector mode: when local vector PMTiles are not ready or fail at runtime, the map does not blank or freeze. It switches to the configured remote raster style for the selected map theme, uses the configured attribution, and continues to support pan, zoom, track display, and track selection. If the environment cannot safely simulate local tile unavailability, mark this row BLOCKED with the missing control. - MAP_15 Manual remote raster source override: in a local-vector deployment, open Map → Map style , switch Map Source from Auto to Remote, and verify the base map reloads from the configured remote raster provider without /api/map-proxy tile requests. OSM raster themes remain selectable, Swiss vector themes are not offered in Remote mode, the setting persists after reload, and Reset restores Auto. - MAP_16 Open the Map overview, then Map style, terrain, personal data, and route-overlay screens. Each Back action restores the overview; summaries reflect the changes. Repeat on a phone and after reload; reset restores defaults without changing the UI theme. ## 3. Track Details - TRD_01 Open at least one GPX-backed track and one FIT-backed track from user-facing navigation (map, browser, or stats) and record the track ids/source filenames. - TRD_02 Opening a track loads its overview, charts, related-tracks list, event list, mini-map, and quality info. - TRD_03 Switch between Overview , Graphs , Quality , Related , and Events ; tabs do not refetch in a loop, lose state, or show blank panels. - TRD_04 Elevation, speed, distance, and gain charts render with readable values. - TRD_05 Graph controls work: time/distance x-axis toggle, range band toggle, point-count slider, and graph-height slider update charts without layout breakage. - TRD_06 Hovering a chart highlights the matching point on the mini-map and hovering the mini-map highlights the chart. No stale cursors remain after leaving either surface. - TRD_07 The track shape preview (small thumbnail) is visible in browser, filters, stats, related tracks, and selection lists. - TRD_08 Download original source file (GPX/FIT/etc.) → file downloads and matches the uploaded one. - TRD_09 Download as GPX → a valid GPX file downloads even if the source was FIT or another format. - TRD_10 Change activity type (e.g. hiking → cycling) → saves successfully; energy/calorie values update automatically. - TRD_11 Energy "what-if" recalculation (custom rider weight, etc.) → updates the displayed values without permanently saving. - TRD_12 Exclude from statistics toggle → the track stops counting in stats overview; re-including it brings it back. - TRD_13 Related tracks show duplicates and previous/next tracks; clicking one navigates to it. - TRD_14 Events tab shows detected stops / GPS gaps where present; selecting an event highlights the matching mini-map position and deselects cleanly. - TRD_15 Open Track Details from Statistics → Tracks and from Filter → Review tracks . Closing details returns to the same originating sheet and list state. Repeat with browser Back/Forward and on narrow mobile; a direct track-detail link closes to the map. The referring panel stays open at a constant height underneath GPS details. Check the latest-activity shortcut and Related track links too; returning must reveal the existing panel without a closing or reopening animation. - TRD_16 Open Quality → GPS review on the synthetic continuity cases. Original and processed paths, source quality, processing decisions, and unsupported intervals remain distinguishable. Selecting a review item highlights its local geometry without connecting disconnected recording spans. - TRD_17 On the synthetic motion cases, compare Overview and Events: moving + stopped + unknown equals elapsed duration for a complete timeline. Short observed pauses count toward stopped time but do not create break events below one minute. Longer breaks show approximate boundaries; missing or invalid time remains unavailable/unknown, not a zero-duration stop. See motion rules . - TRD_18 Local connected Health pass only: compare whole-track and moving heart-rate summaries with their server values. Whole-track heart rate includes recorded stops; moving heart rate uses moving intervals only. Time/distance graphs share the full track extent and preserve partial coverage. A track without samples shows unavailable values and a useful sync-status link. On fresh servers mark NOT APPLICABLE: personal Health account required. - TRD_19 Open a track without Health samples on the fresh server. Core metrics, graphs, mini-map, Quality, and Events remain usable; missing heart rate does not cause repeated requests, blank core charts, or fabricated zero values. ## 4. Filters - FLT_01 Open the filter panel → previously saved filter is still active and shown as a chip. - FLT_02 Browse the filter catalog; search and grouping work. - FLT_03 Choose a filter in Filter view , confirm Use this view , and open Criteria (required missing criteria open automatically). Valid parameter edits auto-apply immediately; clearing or removing parameters resets their effect; active chips, visible count, map, legend, and stats reflect the current state without stale pending UI. - FLT_04 Date, text, and geo parameters all save and re-apply correctly after reload. - FLT_05 Geo drawing : draw a circle, rectangle, and polygon; undo, cancel, finish, and clear all work; saved shapes reappear next time. - FLT_06 Applied filter updates: visible track count, map colors, legend, and stats — without a full page reload. - FLT_07 Legend reflects the active filter (categories or gradient); collapsing/hiding groups updates the map immediately. - FLT_08 Clearing the filter restores all tracks. - FLT_09 Choose a grouped year filter, select two result categories, and verify the map, visible count, track browser, heatmap, Statistics Overview, Trends, and Stats Tracks all use the same selected tracks. - FLT_10 Repeat result-category selection with main activity groups and exact activity types such as Walking and Hiking. Labels and counts remain correct. - FLT_11 Change date, text, or geo parameters while an exact result-category selection is active. The selection remains active; newly discovered categories remain unchecked. - FLT_12 Select none and verify the empty result is intentional and stable. Select every available category and verify it returns to All categories when there are no unavailable saved categories. - FLT_13 Change parameters so a selected category has no matches. It remains visible as unavailable and can be removed. - FLT_14 Switch to a different filter and verify the result-category selection clears. Select the current filter again and verify its selection remains. - FLT_15 Reload with an exact result-category selection. It is restored before the first resolution and all filter-aware views still match. - FLT_16 Hide a group with the map legend visibility control. Map visibility changes, but statistics do not. Changing the global Result categories selection resets temporary legend hiding during map reload. - FLT_17 NOT APPLICABLE in the current UI: automatic first-visit filter guidance was removed. Keep this ID for historical reports; the current overview and on-demand guidance are covered by FLT_18 and FLT_22. - FLT_18 Reopen Filter as a returning user on desktop and narrow mobile. Guidance stays inside the result summary, remains compact without overflow, and More info opens the full explanation without the Important badge. Back returns to Filter; Close closes the sheet. - FLT_19 Pause and resume from the Filtering on / Filtering off switch in the result summary. The result status, map, statistics, persisted state, and switch position remain synchronized on desktop and mobile; no header switch or duplicate action appears. - FLT_20 Open Review tracks from the shared footer beside Show on map . The review uses the same track-browser view as Statistics → Tracks, including search, summary, responsive table/cards, sorting, pagination, map selection, and track details. Recheck Statistics → Tracks after the shared-component change. - FLT_21 Filter and Review tracks use the standard Filter sheet dimensions and detents. Verify the nested review does not jump to an oversized desktop sheet and remains usable at both mobile detents. - FLT_22 Open Filter as a new and returning user. The overview provides Filter view, Criteria, Included categories, Map colors, Review tracks, and Show on map. Open each available inner screen and return with Back. Closing or Show on map keeps the filter active; reopening from the map result count works. - FLT_23 Stage a different Filter view. Compatible criteria are retained; criteria that would be cleared are listed before confirmation. A custom category order shows a notice that it will reset to the new view's default. Cancel preserves the old view and order. Use this view applies the choice, clears old category selection and custom order, and opens missing required criteria without sending an invalid query. - FLT_24 In Criteria, exercise Last 30 days, This year, Last year, and All time. Both date bounds update together. A reversed range shows a field error, disables Done, and retains the last successful map result; correcting it recovers. While paused, valid edits retain their draft and Apply and enable restores the intended result. - FLT_25 Search Included categories, stage a subset, and verify the displayed draft count before Apply while the map remains unchanged. Cancel discards edits; Apply updates map, review, Statistics, heatmap, and Segments consistently. Empty search and zero selected categories provide recovery actions. - FLT_26 Reset a non-default view with criteria, categories, and colors, then Undo while offered. The previous configuration and result return. Map color changes and Show all for hidden map groups leave the statistical track set unchanged. SQL inspection remains a secondary action. - FLT_27 On a narrow phone, complete and cancel circle, rectangle, and polygon drawing from Criteria. Return to Criteria with the correct retained/updated values. Back, Done, Review tracks, and Show on map remain reachable without horizontal scrolling. - FLT_28 In a view with a preferred palette, apply No coloring and reload. The choice survives without changing dates, categories, or matches. Repeat with filtering paused, then resume and switch between category and gradient views. Reset uses the view defaults; Undo restores No coloring. Repeat on desktop and phone. ## 5. Track Browser And Statistics - TBS_01 Track browser lists all (or filtered) tracks with name, date, distance, duration, activity, etc. - TBS_02 Search matches names, descriptions, dates, distances, durations, activity, and file paths. - TBS_03 Sort by each column works; summary row reflects what is currently visible. - TBS_04 Quick-view/preset buttons switch the browser subset correctly and preserve usable sorting/search behavior. - TBS_05 Clicking a row opens the track's details. - TBS_06 Statistics overview shows total distance, time, elevation, activity breakdown, rankings, milestones, and period charts. - TBS_07 Stats are correct for: empty dataset, a single track, and many tracks. - TBS_08 Stats update after the required five-GPX import and again after deleting two imported tracks; no stale deleted-track totals remain. - TBS_09 Time-period charts (daily/weekly/monthly) render and switch correctly. - TBS_10 Clicking a stats entry navigates / filters / highlights as expected. - TBS_11 Highlight drilldowns open the expected track list, open a selected track, and expose excluded-highlight counts where applicable. - TBS_12 Statistics use the same resolved track set as the active filter: apply a geo-drawn filter (circle, rectangle, or polygon) that changes the visible map count, then verify Stats Overview totals, Trends track totals, and the Stats Tracks tab all match the filtered map count. Repeat after a reload to confirm the fallback ID-resolution path still matches. - TBS_13 When Statistics Overview shows Showing X of Y tracks , activate the summary with pointer and keyboard. It opens Filter directly on desktop and mobile. - TBS_14 Open Statistics → Trends → Charts . Media is the final chart; All media is selected by default in the control at the top. Both choices expose visible, keyboard-accessible help. The choice is shared with Map settings → Your data and Overview media counts. - TBS_15 Change grouping and sub-unit. Activity and media periods remain aligned, with zero values where needed. Apply date, category, geographic and custom filters: media follows the earliest valid start and latest valid end of the actual matching tracks, including gaps and both endpoints. Older, newer and undated media never appear. Empty/undated track selections show no media. All media includes unlinked items; Track related additionally requires a selected link to a matching track. Map markers refresh with both filter and scope changes, and stale requests cannot restore old markers. - TBS_16 Select a non-empty photo or video stack. The period mosaic uses the same track-defined range and opens with the correct total, All/Photos/Videos filters, stable newest-first cards, 60-item Load more pages, recoverable loading/error states, and shared viewer navigation. In Track related scope, Open activity returns to that activity's Media tab; the action is absent in All media scope. There is no undated drill-down. - TBS_17 Open Statistics and each Overview, Trends, and Tracks entry. Back returns to the hub and restores focus; track search, sorting, and Trends controls survive the round trip. The latest-activity preview respects the current track set, opens details, and handles an empty set. - TBS_18 Change Trends chart height and order, reload, and restore defaults. The saved layout returns, height stays usable within the viewport, and the media chart remains included. Repeat on a narrow phone in light and dark themes. ## 6. Planner - PLN_01 Open Planner → Start a new plan (or Continue your current plan when a draft exists); pick a routing profile (e.g. hiking or touring bike). - PLN_02 Click on the map to add waypoints → a route is computed and drawn. - PLN_03 Insert a waypoint on an existing leg by dragging the route. - PLN_04 Move and delete waypoints; clear, undo, and redo all work. - PLN_05 Live stats bar (distance, ascent, time) updates as you edit. - PLN_06 Elevation profile renders and hovering it highlights the matching map point. - PLN_07 Save plan , list saved plans, load a saved plan, delete a plan. - PLN_08 Download plan as GPX → file is valid and matches the planned route. - PLN_09 If the routing engine (BRouter) is missing data for an area, the UI shows a clear "segment downloading / unavailable" state instead of an unhandled error. - PLN_10 Existing planned routes still display even when the planner has trouble fetching new data. - PLN_11 Touch dragging on mobile works for placing and moving waypoints. - PLN_12 From the Planner hub, open the contextual guide, return, draw a draft, and return to the hub again. The draft survives; map clicks edit only in the drawing screen. Saved plans and drawing remain reachable on desktop and mobile. - PLN_13 Select numbered waypoints and exercise tap-to-move, cancel move, insertion, removal, reverse, and trim before/after. Undo/redo restores geometry, stats, and routing profile. Drag release must not add an extra point; point actions remain reachable on touch screens. - PLN_14 Search and open a saved plan. Its exact saved geometry, profile, notes, and stats load and the map frames it above the panel. With an unsaved draft, cancel replacement and confirm the draft survives; then explicitly replace it. Loading failures offer retry without silently clearing the draft. - PLN_15 Save after an edit while routing is pending. Save waits for current geometry and prevents duplicate submission. A failed save keeps name/notes for retry. Editing a saved plan offers Save copy and leaves the original intact; success offers a working GPX download. A backend 200 alone is not evidence of browser file delivery. - PLN_16 With unsaved changes, attempt to leave/reload the page and cancel the browser prompt. The draft remains. Trigger a slow route request, then change profile, clear, undo, or load a saved plan; a late reply must not overwrite the newer state. - PLN_17 On desktop and phone, use More map , Show tools , slow and fast panel drags, and grabber taps. Totals, profile, and Undo stay visible without scrolling; the profile stays readable and its map cursor aligned until the totals-only size. Downward flicks never close the drawing panel, the chosen size returns on the next visit, and route updates keep the previous totals until the new result arrives. ## 7. Measuring And Comparison Tools - MCT_01 Open Segments , place start and end zones, and choose Analyze → crossing attempts appear with speed/time/distance. - MCT_02 Clicking a result opens that track's details / segment view. - MCT_03 Stop the measure tool → all temporary markers and listeners are cleaned up. - MCT_04 Segment comparison: pick several tracks → comparison chart + map align them correctly even with missing data. - MCT_05 Sub-track / segment extraction (between two points on a track) returns the expected slice. - MCT_06 Segment geometry sanity: after selecting a measured segment, the comparison map line stays within the selected tracks' real local bounds. There must be no straight global line, jump to [0,0], or off-continent segment such as a line toward South Africa. - MCT_07 Place multiple ordered zones, adjust the radius, undo a zone, and Analyze. Zone counts and the results describe the same filtered tracks. Empty results explain how to adjust the selection; editing zones invalidates the old analysis. - MCT_08 Using repeated-visit fixtures, select individual attempts and a reference, then switch among result table, charts, and Replay. Labels, colors, reference, and exact zone/visit identities stay consistent; Select all is explicit. Consolidated summaries retain separate valid visit counts for each metric. - MCT_09 Compare exact attempt boundaries, distance, elapsed time, energy, ascent/descent, and power with server results for the synthetic fixtures. Changing chart density changes presentation only. Fractional boundary work must not include whole-track energy outside the segment. See segment rules . - MCT_10 Analyze missing/repeated/reversed-time and recording-gap cases. Untimed attempts remain inspectable where geometry permits; unavailable timing is labelled rather than ranked as zero. Core charts preserve gaps and supported partial coverage without inventing a bridge. - MCT_11 On a fixture with a recorded stop, compare finish faster/slower labels and Time difference at equal traveled distance . The latter stays on a distance axis, includes stopped time, ends at shared coverage, and is not described as spatial lead/lag. - MCT_12 Inspect aligned graphs by hover, click-to-pin, keyboard, and touch. The shared value panel and map position agree; selecting an attempt from the whole value card updates highlighting. The panel sits beside charts when space permits and below them on a phone. - MCT_13 Local connected Health pass only: verify segment HR, coverage, cardiac cost, and unavailable reasons against server values for matching local samples. Ordinary HR includes recorded stops; cardiac cost uses covered moving intervals including coasting. Consolidated HR uses covered-time weighting. On fresh servers mark NOT APPLICABLE: personal Health account required. - MCT_14 On a fresh server without Health data, selected core results, charts, and replay still load. Missing Health results remain unavailable. Retry a failed core attempt without losing other selected results; rapidly changing selection must not restore stale responses. - MCT_15 Reimport or remove a disposable synthetic source after discovery, or let its attempt reference expire. Rows match the selected filters without duplicates. Date-only records retain their calendar date. Test responsive cards/table and unknown/null values when present in local data. - GHL_13 Observe an ordinary background sync. Current pass/window progress stays distinct from cumulative mirror counts; the verified snapshot age remains visible during work and counts refresh after the cycle stops. Pending history and retry ranges link to Processing. Do not force a reconnect, full-history sync, failure, or cancellation on the owner's account merely to satisfy this row. - GHL_14 When an existing exercise has an imported route, open the associated track and exercise-only scope. The matching route is shown, ordinary statistics stay consistent, and normal repeated background sync does not duplicate it. Record missing eligible routes as a local data prerequisite. - GHL_15 Switch metric/US customary units and light/dark themes across Health, track HR, and segment HR/cardiac cost. Distances, weight, and speed convert where applicable; bpm, watts, and beats/kJ retain their meaning. Coverage/unavailable labels and charts stay readable at phone width. Restore the owner's original preferences. ### Synthetic synchronization acceptance Use an isolated database and synthetic provider responses for these checks. Do not reload, reset, or mutate the owner's connected mirror. - Fast work runs first, full work advances across bounded cycles and restart, and busy ticks create no replay. Show incomplete fast coverage under overload. - Named corrections and timestamp moves retain one current identity; differing nameless observations survive. Invalid/conflicting pages cannot replace records. - Complete children sweep only their own bounds/stamps, including NULL stamps; empty days finalize, revoked owners fail, and rollback leaves no final mark. - Empty batches write daily audits, stop at gaps/caps, and shrink when data appears. A 1970 floor with parked gaps remains responsive through cached status. - Range/all reload supersedes matching finals without pre-deletion. Unrequested parked portions remain parked. Retry releases failures; reset clears every new state. - Exercise removal retains files, owners, and associations. Reappearance and track replacement reuse ownership. Adding location permission exports stored routes. - Persist Retry-After cooldown; count all HTTP attempts, probes, retries, and decoded response bytes. Record real-account envelope, density, delay, and cost measurements separately before making production performance claims. ## Suggested Regression Passes | Pass | Scope | |---|---| | Smoke (~10 min) | Sign-in, map loads, apply filter, open a track, open stats, open planner, sign out. | | Full desktop | All applicable coverage IDs above on a desktop browser with a normal network. | | Full mobile / touch | Applicable mobile checks for SGN, MAP, TRD, FLT, TBS, PLN, MCT, AVR, MED, ADM, GPS, GHL, and MOB; connected Health remains local-only. | | Offline / cache | NET_01-NET_05; offline reload (NET_01) and service-worker update (NET_04) require installed web-app mode. Cached basemap outage/recovery (NET_05), network recovery, and authentication checks also apply to ordinary tabs. | | Data-change | DAT, IMP, FIT, DEL, MED_06-MED_44, and SYN: import, conversion, track and media deletion flows, persisted media correlation, video playback, compatible streaming, bounded temporary storage, freshness, cache refresh, map, browser, statistics, responsive viewer, large-library paging, and media audit. | | Theme | APP_01-APP_08: toggle dark/light and each map style; verify UI, charts, map, and persistence. | | Locale and units | LOC_01-LOC_05: verify locale formatting and persistence, then run the metric/imperial conversion and persistence flow. | | Remote raster maps | MAP_13-MAP_15: intentional remote tile mode, per-theme provider URLs and attribution, local-vector fallback when tiles are unavailable, and the manual Remote map source override. | | UX performance | UXP_01: repeat the core desktop journey with browser responsiveness and first-party API timing capture. | | Navigation and editing | MAP_16, FLT_22-FLT_27, TBS_17-TBS_18, PLN_12-PLN_17, ADM_13-ADM_15, MOB_07-MOB_08. | | Segment and motion | DAT_09, TRD_16-TRD_17, TRD_19, MCT_07-MCT_12, MCT_14-MCT_15, AVR_05-AVR_06; synthetic/public fixtures on the fresh server. | | Google Health fresh-server | GHL_01-GHL_02, GHL_04-GHL_06; no personal account. Mark connected rows NOT APPLICABLE with the local-account reason. | | Google Health local connected | GHL_07-GHL_15, TRD_18, MCT_13; existing local account, available records, redacted evidence. GHL_03 account mutations require separate explicit authorization. |

title: Codex /goal Launcher
text: # Codex /goal Launcher ## Problem The full MTL Explorer regression has too much detail for one self-contained launcher prompt. Agents also tend to stop midway, compress the checklist, or pick only the parts they consider most important when the run is not resumable. ## Approach Use this file only as the short Goal launcher. Keep the detailed instructions in documentation/development/testing/full-regression/start.md and have the Goal read them from the repository. - Initialize the run and frozen coverage queue with the workflow script. - Split the run into one packet per coverage ID. - Save packet results and evidence as files. - Track progress in run-state.md. - Assemble the final report only from completed packet files. The /goal job is the coordinator loop: pick the next packet, run it, save state, and continue or resume later. ## How To Start 1. Prepare a fresh disposable server with root SSH access. 2. Open Codex at the repository root. 3. Replace the server and temporary SSH credential placeholders. Do not commit real credentials. 4. Copy the complete Goal Prompt below, including its initial /goal, into Codex. 5. The agent should run workflow/init-run.py, use the printed run folder, and work through the frozen coverage IDs in that run's coverage-plan.md. To resume a stopped run, use: ## Goal Prompt

title: Full Regression Packet Template
text: # Full Regression Packet Template Copy this template to ../mtl-explorer-private/docs-my/verification/regression/full-suite/<YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM-short-slug>/packets/<coverage-id>.md for each coverage packet. Use the same shape for RUN_SETUP.md and RUN_CLEANUP.md. ## Completion Rules - Each packet covers one coverage ID and must have an explicit status. - PASS requires direct action and evidence, not a broad prefix summary. - New findings start as OPEN. Use FIX_IN_WORK only after an owner starts implementing, reviewing, or directly verifying a fix; regression investigation or triage alone is not fix work. - FIXED requires direct retest evidence that a previously recorded issue now behaves as expected. - REJECTED requires a concrete reason that the candidate issue is expected behavior, invalid, or outside the coverage requirement. - NOT REPRODUCEABLE or NOT REPRODUCIBLE requires direct evidence that the recorded reproduction path was attempted and did not reproduce the issue. Prefer NOT REPRODUCIBLE for new entries; the gate accepts both spellings. - PARTIAL must name the missing child checks and keep the coverage ID resumable in run-state.md. - NOT COVERED means the coverage ID still lacks direct execution evidence; it is resumable during a normal full regression, not a terminal packet result. - BLOCKED must explain the dependency, permission, service, data, or tooling constraint and whether it blocks the full regression. - NOT APPLICABLE must explain why the coverage text does not apply to this configured run. - Evidence should be compact: WebP screenshots where useful, each WebP screenshot asset at 85 KB (85,000 bytes) or less, .txt log snippets under 5 KB, and no bulky traces unless needed for a failure. - Every packet evidence asset reference must be a Markdown link. From packet files, use ../assets/<filename> as the href while keeping the visible label as assets/<filename>. - Embed packet WebP screenshots inline with Markdown image syntax in Screenshot Evidence; link text/log evidence instead of pasting long content. - If the packet mutates shared state, record the before and after state in the packet and in run-state.md.
