title: Resumable Full Regression Workflow
text: # Resumable Full Regression Workflow Use this workflow for evidence-heavy MTL Explorer full regressions that are too large for one continuous agent run. The goal is simple: one packet per coverage ID, saved state, and one final report assembled from packet results. There is no separate packet catalog. For each new run, init-run.py copies documentation/development/testing/full-regression/coverage-plan.md to the run folder as coverage-plan.md. That snapshot is the frozen queue, read top to bottom. New coverage applies to newly initialized runs. Do not rewrite historical plan snapshots, packet outcomes, or verification reports when updating the source plan. Fresh-server runs do not use a personal Google Health account. The source plan separates disabled/unconfigured/demo checks from local connected checks. Record each local-only row as NOT APPLICABLE with the account prerequisite and retain its packet. This is a scope exclusion, not an unfinished item or evidence of a successful account sync. Connected checks use only the existing local account in a separate pass; account lifecycle mutations require explicit authorization. ## Sources - README.md: quick-install commands, URLs, credentials, prerequisites, and import-folder paths. - documentation/development/testing/full-regression/coverage-plan.md: coverage IDs, coverage text, and packet order used to initialize a new run. - <run-folder>/coverage-plan.md: frozen coverage queue for one run. - documentation/development/testing/full-regression/packet-template.md: required packet result format. - documentation/tools/testing/full-regression/init-run.py: run-folder, plan-snapshot, and queue initializer. - docker/gpx_porto_taxi_dataset/photo_placeholder.py: shared demo and regression photo renderer, packaged at /app/demo/photo_placeholder.py. - docker/gpx_porto_taxi_dataset/generate_regression_photos.py: packaged entry point for the disposable JPEG and video set plus matching synthetic GPX activity. ## How To Start Evidence lives in the separate sibling mtl-explorer-private checkout. Set MTL_PRIVATE_REPO for another private checkout, or use --output-root for a standalone run. The application checkout does not need private files for builds or automated tests. 1. Prepare a fresh disposable server with root SSH access. 2. Copy the prompt block from documentation/development/testing/full-regression/start.md. 3. Replace the server IP, temporary SSH credential, and app-image placeholders in the copied prompt. Do not commit real credentials. 4. Start /goal, or another long-running agent run, with the filled prompt. 5. Run the initializer exactly once before testing: 6. Use the run folder printed by the initializer for all state, packets, and evidence. To resume a stopped run, start the agent with: ## Run Folder Create one run folder with init-run.py before testing starts: The initializer uses HHMM as the run start time in 24-hour local time, for example 2026-05-25_1430-quick-install-full-regression. It records the source plan path, repository Git revision, SHA-256 of the snapshot, target, app image, and every coverage queue row in run-state.md. Only create report.md after the finalization gate below passes, or after the user explicitly approves closing the run with remaining coverage gaps. ## Ordering - Run RUN_SETUP first: install MTL Explorer, record README facts, URLs, credentials source, environment, baseline state, and access details. - Then work coverage IDs from the run's coverage-plan.md top to bottom. - Do not skip ahead unless the current ID is terminal or explicitly needs later app state. - Import/data IDs naturally prepare the shared dataset for later UI IDs. - Track delete IDs run after all IDs that need the full imported track dataset. - MED_06 creates and indexes the disposable media dataset before MED_01. Run MED_07-MED_12 only after MED_40; keep deletion backups and the fixture manifest outside the watched media tree. - Run RUN_CLEANUP last: final report, evidence audit, stack shutdown, and disposable-directory removal. ## Endless Coverage Gate The run is intentionally resumable and should keep going across context compaction, agent restarts, or handoffs. Do not convert unfinished executable coverage into a terminal result just to produce a report. ### Status Semantics - Terminal statuses for normal queue advancement: PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, NOT APPLICABLE, FIXED, REJECTED, NOT REPRODUCEABLE, and NOT REPRODUCIBLE. - Resumable statuses: NOT STARTED, IN PROGRESS, PARTIAL, and NOT COVERED. - PARTIAL means some direct evidence exists, but required child behavior is still missing. Leave enough handoff notes for the next agent to continue. - NOT COVERED means no direct execution evidence exists yet. In an active run, it is a queue marker, not a completed result. - Use BLOCKED only when a concrete dependency, permission, service, data set, browser capability, or environment constraint prevents execution in this run. Record what would unblock it. - Use NOT APPLICABLE only when the coverage text genuinely does not apply to the configured run, such as plain-HTTP live geolocation checks on a remote non-localhost origin. - Use FIXED only when retesting a previously recorded issue proves the expected behavior now works. - Use REJECTED only when a candidate issue is closed as expected behavior, invalid, or outside the coverage requirement, with the reason recorded. - Use NOT REPRODUCEABLE or NOT REPRODUCIBLE only when the tester attempted the recorded reproduction path and could not reproduce the issue. Prefer NOT REPRODUCIBLE for new entries; the gate accepts both spellings. ### Finding Status Semantics Finding statuses are separate from coverage statuses: - OPEN: the finding is confirmed and no fix task is actively working on it. - FIX_IN_WORK: an owner has started implementing, reviewing, or directly verifying a fix. Do not use it for regression investigation or triage alone. - FIXED: direct retest evidence proves the expected behavior works. - REJECTED: the finding was closed as expected behavior, invalid, or outside the coverage requirement, with the reason recorded. - NOT REPRODUCIBLE: the recorded reproduction path was attempted and did not reproduce the issue. NOT REPRODUCEABLE remains accepted for legacy runs. Change OPEN to FIX_IN_WORK when the fix task actually starts. Change it to a terminal finding state only when the required evidence exists. If work stops without a terminal outcome, return the finding to OPEN. FIX_IN_WORK is not a coverage status and does not by itself block regression report assembly. ### Resume Selection When resuming, pick the first row in queue order whose status is one of: If run-state.md says Current coverage ID: COMPLETE but any row still has one of those resumable statuses, the state is inconsistent. Correct Current coverage ID and Next coverage ID to the first resumable row and continue. ### Finalization Gate Before creating report.md, setting Current coverage ID: COMPLETE, or running RUN_CLEANUP, audit the queue: - Every coverage ID from the run's coverage-plan.md must have a packet. - No packet or run-state row may remain NOT STARTED, IN PROGRESS, PARTIAL, or NOT COVERED. - Any unexecuted-but-required item must remain resumable, not be summarized away. - If an item cannot execute, convert it to BLOCKED or NOT APPLICABLE with a precise reason and unblock path. For issue-retest outcomes, use FIXED, REJECTED, or NOT REPRODUCIBLE only with direct retest evidence. - If the user explicitly requests early closure with gaps, record that approval in Final Assembly Notes, keep the result FAIL, and then cleanup may proceed. If the gate fails and there is no explicit early-closure approval, do not create the final report and do not run cleanup. Update run-state.md so the next resumable coverage ID is visible. Run the gate checker before final report/cleanup: The checker must print Finalization gate: PASS for normal cleanup. A failing checker result means the run is still resumable. The checker uses the run's coverage-plan.md, not the current workspace plan. For a legacy run without a snapshot, it uses the coverage rows already recorded in that run's run-state.md and prints a warning. ## Coordinator Rules - The lead/coordinator owns run-state.md and final report.md. - Each coverage packet covers exactly one coverage ID. - Name packet files as packets/<coverage-id>.md, for example packets/TRD_01.md. - Packet workers only edit their own packet file and matching assets/<coverage-id>-* files. - A packet is terminal only when its coverage ID has action, expected result, actual result, status, and evidence for a terminal status. PARTIAL and NOT COVERED packets are handoff packets and remain resumable during a normal full regression. - If a packet stops midway, leave its status as IN PROGRESS or BLOCKED in run-state.md and include handoff notes in the packet file. ## Run State Template init-run.py creates run-state.md in this shape: Use coverage statuses consistently: NOT STARTED, IN PROGRESS, PASS, PARTIAL, FAIL, BLOCKED, NOT COVERED, NOT APPLICABLE, FIXED, REJECTED, NOT REPRODUCEABLE, or NOT REPRODUCIBLE. For queue advancement, PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, NOT APPLICABLE, FIXED, REJECTED, NOT REPRODUCEABLE, and NOT REPRODUCIBLE are terminal unless the user approved early closure with gaps. ## Final Report The final report must keep the existing full-regression format: - First line: > **RESULT: PASS - <one concise reason>** or > **RESULT: FAIL - <one concise reason>**. - Include goal, scope, environment, README facts, setup/install result, timings, coverage-ID matrix, issues, evidence, cleanup, blocked/untested areas, and conclusion. - Assemble the coverage matrix by coverage ID from packet files only. Do not invent final statuses from memory. - Use PASS only if quick install succeeds, required coverage runs, cleanup succeeds, and no blocking/high-severity failures remain. - Do not assemble a final report for a normal run while any coverage ID is still NOT STARTED, IN PROGRESS, PARTIAL, or NOT COVERED. Continue or leave the run resumable instead. A gap report is allowed only after explicit user-approved early closure and must be FAIL.

title: Google Health import simulation
text: # Google Health import simulation The simulator calls Java objects directly. It uses no HTTP, OAuth, Mockito or Spring application startup. The real importer, point mapper, PostgreSQL repository, transactions and database migrations remain in use. GoogleHealthProvider is the data-query contract. Production ApiClient and test SyntheticGoogleHealthProvider implement it. Exercise exports and route work have separate interfaces. SyncService accepts a Java Clock; production uses UTC wall time and the simulation fixes the historical cutoff. ## Dataset The calibrated benchmark delivers 2025-12-11 through 2026-01-01 , with the end excluded: 21 days and 524,400 samples. The original two-year dataset remains available through standard() for correctness and larger-scale experiments. Only raw heart rate contains data: - One synthetic band, sampled every three seconds. - A band-off gap every seven days, with fixed random seed 73421 . Gaps start at a random time on the first day of each seven-day period and last 2–36 hours, including gaps across midnight. The benchmark has three gaps. - String BPM, physical timestamps, UTC offsets, civil date/time and device metadata. Europe/Zurich offsets follow daylight-saving transitions. - Resource names are absent by default, matching the sampled Google record structure. Smaller correctness cases also exercise named records and multiple sources. The provider allocates one page at a time. Samples are stable across overlapping queries and worker restarts. No NAS records or credentials are stored in fixtures. transformSamples, beforeRead and responseDelay support corrections, removals, expired tokens, quota pauses and delayed reads. expectedSamples provides the expected count after gaps. ## Run Run Maven in the existing development container. Build a current source snapshot under its external-drive workspace mount, as with other backend checks. Provider checks need no database: Database checks require a disposable PostGIS database whose name starts with mtl_health_simulation. The harness resets its Google Health mirror. Provision a separate database named mtl in the same isolated cluster: an existing production migration grants a read-only role access to that literal database name. Use the existing development PostGIS image with the standard database settings , and stop the temporary container after checks. Pass these environment variables into the development container: These tests import a short portion of the standard dataset and smaller recovery fixtures. They check finalization, persisted page resumption and expired-token splitting. Correction and removal cases use explicit reloads. HistoricalBatchImportSimulationTest also checks unchanged-row retries, retained rows after empty answers, durable duplicate validation and atomic rollback of pages and finalization. Database checks skip when the URL is absent. Compile once before benchmarking, so compilation is outside the timing: The benchmark is opt-in and bounded to one minute. Run this inside the development container: The benchmark truncates the disposable Health schema and resets sequences before each import. The importer gets a 57-second cycle budget and the test has a 60-second timeout. A run must finalize all 21 historical days and store exactly 524,400 samples. An interrupted or incomplete run fails and is not a performance result. The command above also limits the entire prepared test invocation, including JVM startup and cleanup. Output is a JSON report with dates, seed, workload fingerprint, row/day counts, elapsed time, provider generation time, transaction time, commits and read count. Elapsed time covers import and final count verification. Transaction time includes all work inside transactions; it is not pure SQL execution time. Automatic history normalizes pages before the write transaction, so compare total elapsed time as well as transaction time across implementations. Provider byte counters are zero because no responses are decoded. Add -Dmtl.health.simulation.report=/workspace/<external-drive-workspace>/baseline.json to save the report. The fixed workload fingerprint is 80b9e1ec43e0d8ab977a86d56b0b4d556d394ff07739283ed2b671c1318ab7d7. Keep the dates, seed, sample interval, page size and provider implementation unchanged when comparing import improvements. Do not automatically resize the workload to fill the minute after an optimization. -Dmtl.health.simulation.history-days=<days> is an explicit calibration override and changes the workload fingerprint. Tests clear their mirror after the class finishes. The benchmark also truncates its data after timing. Add -Dmtl.health.simulation.keep-data=true to a standalone benchmark run to retain its database rows for further experiments. Do not combine that option with other database suites. Other granted streams return empty pages, so the runner includes the production scheduler's empty-stream work. It does not reproduce Google network latency, response parsing, quotas or NAS disk performance. Use identical settings and storage when comparing algorithm changes. Keep database files and build output on the mounted external drive.

title: Public GPX Regression Deck
text: # Public GPX Regression Deck MTL Explorer keeps a small public GPX regression deck in mtl-server/src/test/resources/gpx/public-regression. The deck uses CC0 fixtures from https://www.viewmygpx.com/sample-gpx-files/. They are synthetic, realistic GPX files with no real user data. Private tracks must not be added to this deck. The tests first audit the source GPX directly, then run the MTL Explorer import path. This is intentional: a source problem should fail separately from a processing regression. Current invariants: - Source point counts, track counts, and waypoint counts match the manifest. - Source timestamps are monotonic inside each segment. - Source adjacent distances stay within plausible bounds. - Imported clean tracks preserve realistic length and point counts. - Imported tracks do not contain impossible adjacent jumps. - Short multi-point glitches are rejected at 10 Hz (60 m) and 5 Hz (100 m). Millisecond fix pairs recover when normal cadence resumes; a real observation gap during probation receives bounded time credit without accumulating cluster time. - Intentional multi-day files split into a small number of substantial tracks, not hundreds of one-point fragments. - Duplicate timestamps retain supported geometry and motion totals without a pending review task. A backward clock beyond one second requires review. - An isolated backward alert preserves supported section timing. Systemic clocks remain contained after reassessment. Reimport rebuilds previously contained timing under current criteria without removing valid alerts. - A supported isolated forward clock spike produces one incident and excludes only its canonical timestamp; RAW timestamps and supported intervals stay available. - Routine denoising never creates aggregate distance, ascent or descent review. Stored aggregate-impact summaries resolve even after limited reassessment, preserving unrelated unchecked issues and acknowledgements; large per-point corrections and substantial rejection retain their review criteria. - Review severity is based on section coverage and measured impact; ordinary pauses and isolated resolved corrections remain informational.

title: Indexer regression cases
text: # Indexer regression cases Use this checklist for changes to file discovery, indexing, removal, restart recovery, or indexer progress. Run it against disposable GPS and media roots with a fresh database and fully synthetic files. Keep GPS and media results separate; shared indexer behavior can still differ at the watcher, importer, or domain-data layers. For the core cases, test live changes while the server runs and offline changes followed by startup catch-up. Use a separate database and roots for each mode. Do not use a manual rescan to turn a missed automatic event into a pass. ## Core cases | ID | Case | Expected result | | --- | --- | --- | | IDX-01 | Add files while the server is running. | Each file is durably scheduled, processed, and represented once in domain data. | | IDX-02 | Remove indexed files while the server is running. | Derived records are cleaned up and the index record reaches its removed state. | | IDX-03 | Change an indexed file while the server is running. | The latest revision is imported; stale derived data and duplicate records are absent. | | IDX-04 | Add a batch, then forcibly stop the server with discovered work pending. Restart with the same database and roots. Repeat with a stop during processing. | Pending work resumes and settles once, without lost or duplicate domain data. Record the stop point and persisted state. | | IDX-05 | Finish indexing, stop the server, change files, and restart. | Startup discovery catches each offline add, removal, and modification without a manual rescan. | Run IDX-01 through IDX-05 for both GPS and media. Keep the offline mutations in separate stop/change/restart phases so later changes cannot hide an earlier miss. ## Additional cases | ID | Case | Expected result | | --- | --- | --- | | IDX-06 | Rescan an unchanged tree. | No unnecessary reprocessing, duplicate records, or status churn. | | IDX-07 | Add a burst of files in nested folders, including equal names in different folders and paths with spaces or Unicode. | Every included path is handled once and remains distinct. | | IDX-08 | Rename or move files into the watched tree; atomically replace an existing path with a temporary file. | New paths are indexed and old or replaced content is cleaned up without duplicates. | | IDX-09 | Change a file repeatedly while its first import is active. | The latest revision is processed after the active operation, with no stale completion overwriting it. | | IDX-10 | Remove a file while it is being indexed. | No stale import remains after cleanup settles. | | IDX-11 | Remove and recreate a file at the same path before cleanup completes. | An older delete cannot remove data for the restored source. | | IDX-12 | Copy a file slowly so discovery may happen before the copy finishes. | Partial content is not accepted as the final indexed revision; processing recovers when the copy completes. | | IDX-13 | Make the source root unavailable or unreadable, then restore it and rescan. | An incomplete scan does not infer mass deletion; indexing recovers when the root is available. | | IDX-14 | Mutate a mounted folder from the host and from inside the server's filesystem environment. | Record which operations deliver watcher events for that mount. A manual rescan is a separate fallback result, not a live-watch pass. | | IDX-15 | Rewrite a file in place with the same size and restore its original modification time. | Record whether the current source-revision contract detects it; document any limitation rather than counting it as ordinary modification coverage. | | IDX-16 | Add malformed, empty, unsupported, or temporarily unreadable files, then correct a failed file. | Failures are visible, do not block unrelated files, and corrected files can be retried. | | IDX-17 | Exercise excluded paths, excluded extensions, and symlinks if they occur in supported deployments. | Excluded or unsupported paths do not create unintended imports or recursive scans. | | IDX-18 | Cause temporary discovery or completion persistence failures; stop between discovery, import, and completion persistence where practical. | Work is not dispatched before discovery is durable; committed work remains recoverable and visible. | | IDX-19 | Build a large backlog behind a slow import and inspect status through the admin UI. | Counts include the full backlog, discovery and processing are distinguishable, and progress settles correctly. | | IDX-20 | Verify the client after new data is indexed or removed. | Freshness notification and reload/reconnect show the settled server state. | ## Evidence For every case, record the index (GPS or media), detection mode, source paths, mutation and settlement times, index status, invocation or generation information when available, domain-data counts, and relevant logs. Capture the admin UI when status or freshness behavior is part of the assertion. Use synthetic files only; keep generated files, database state, and other bulky run data outside the repository. For an end-to-end run, follow the repository's mtl-test-indexer skill. Keep dated results and screenshots in private verification evidence; this page is the reusable case catalog.

title: Photo handling improvement verification
text: # Photo handling improvement verification Focused local verification for the Track Details photo timeline, server-side activity matching, camera offsets, mini-map positions, and enhanced media viewer. Use only public tracks and fully synthetic media. Do not use local personal GPX tracks or photos as fixtures or evidence. ## Reusable regression data Run docker/gpx_porto_taxi_dataset/generate_regression_photos.py <output-dir> in the app container or a Python environment with Pillow, piexif, ffmpeg, and ffprobe. It creates six small synthetic JPEGs, a short H.264/AAC MP4, a short H.264/AAC MOV, a manifest, and mtl-regression-media-track.gpx. Four photos and the MP4 contain embedded GPS. Two photos and the MOV contain camera time only and should resolve to the matching GPX route. The GPS points are near, but not identical to, the track points. For the full installed-app flow, follow the copy/index order in full regression start instructions . Run the focused frontend regression with: For thumbnail recovery, cover a burst of 120 uncached photos with a busy converter, opening despite a failed preview, retry on activation, keyboard and touch activation, and cancellation when leaving the collection or hiding thumbnails. Verify that a cached preview loads during thumbnail conversion, an uncached preview survives 60 seconds of converter contention, and queued thumbnails wait across preview retries. Check activity photos, the media mosaic, and the filmstrip in light and dark themes. A filmstrip drag must not restart recovery or select a photo.

Replace the placeholders before sending. bash mkdir mtl-explorer cd mtl-explorer curl -fsSL -o docker-compose.yml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mindalyze-com/mtl-explorer/main/docker-compose.yml docker compose up -d `

title: End-user regression
text: # End-user regression A full regression uses a frozen coverage plan, one packet per coverage ID, a resumable run state, and a final report. Keep completed outcomes and source snapshots as dated evidence. Reusable workflow and tooling are linked from the full-regression instructions . The current coverage plan defines new runs; an existing run uses its own snapshot. Follow the stable test identifier standard for browser checks. Normally add missing IDs in the application instead of XPath or fragile CSS/positional selectors. Clear scoped roles and labels remain valid; document necessary exceptions for installed releases or canvas interactions. Focused indexer checks cover live filesystem changes and startup catch-up after offline changes. Use the indexer regression cases and the repository's indexer skill for that workflow. Preserve working-function screenshots as well as failures. New runs use public or synthetic files and temporary services with restart disabled. Connected personal-account Health checks require their existing local prerequisites and keep personal values out of evidence.

title: Security checks
text: # Security checks Review the actual trust boundary affected by the change: authenticated APIs, source-file access, OAuth state and identity, token storage, downloads, or operator-owned upstream configuration. Verify rejected access and malformed input without printing credentials or personal payloads. Account consent and callback rules belong to the authorization contract . Use the security policy for reporting. Keep private findings and reproduction details in internal verification until a public disclosure is explicitly authorized. Dated security results are kept in internal verification; they do not certify a later build.

title: Unit and integration checks
text: # Unit and integration checks Run Java checks in the existing development container. Use the Maven lifecycle so diagnostics and consumers rebuild together. Backend database tests use the standard database settings with isolated storage and credentials. Frontend tests run through npm test in mtl-client/. Select the affected Vitest suites for a focused check, then run type checking and the relevant build. Test observable contracts: supported and unavailable measurements, input/output shapes, request cancellation, boundaries, and failure recovery. Do not add tests that only repeat implementation statements. When API shape changes, export the live OpenAPI schema, regenerate its client, and verify server/client agreement. See the API workflow .

title: Video transcoding verification
text: # Video transcoding verification Use this focused regression to verify browser-compatible video fallback without committing media fixtures. Generate native fixtures with docker/gpx_porto_taxi_dataset/generate_regression_photos.py. Generate an archival-codec case in a temporary directory with ffmpeg, for example FFV1 or ProRes video with PCM audio in a MOV container. Browser codec support varies. If the test browser plays the archival codec, use a temporary local harness that gives the production player a naturally unsupported source while its transcode request points to the indexed synthetic video. Do not simulate the media error in page code. Keep the harness and generated files out of Git and remove them after the run. Verify: - native MP4 playback does not create a transcode session; - decode/source errors offer Auto, 480p, 720p, and 1080p compatible playback; - network errors retain the normal media retry path; - progress, slow conversion, cancellation, retry, and original download remain usable; - HLS playback reaches the full generated duration; - reopening the same media revision and quality reuses prepared work; - one active session, one completed result, byte/runtime limits, expiry, eviction, and startup cleanup bound temporary disk use; - no generated video is added to Git. Record automated commands, ffprobe output, browser evidence, temporary storage measurements, session reuse, cleanup, and any findings under ../mtl-explorer-private/docs-my/verification/features/<YYYY-MM-DD-video>/. Keep raw videos on the mounted external drive; link only compact report evidence.

title: Website and documentation
text: # Website and documentation The product website lives in docs/. Documentation sources live under the audience folders in documentation/. - Author and organize documentation - User documentation style - Generate, check, and preview the site - Capture and maintain screenshots - Analytics - Release-note authoring Generated pages are committed with their sources. Publication remains a separate, explicitly requested action through ../mtl-explorer-private/publish-to-github.py.

title: Web analytics
text: # Web analytics Umami analytics is intended only for public MTL Explorer demo instances. It is off by default on all installations, including demos. Each selected demo must opt in explicitly; demo mode alone does not enable analytics. Private installations should leave analytics disabled and can omit both the script URL and website ID. They need no Umami script, window.umami object, analytics server or external network access for this integration. The client checks only its own server's public configuration endpoint. Disabled or incomplete settings load no external script or analytics hook. Add these environment variables to the app container , then restart it: The equivalent server settings are mtl.analytics.umami.enabled, script-url and website-id in application.yml. Use the website ID for this installation from Umami. The ID is public; dashboard credentials and API tokens are not needed. The script URL must use HTTPS without credentials, query parameters or fragments. Missing or invalid settings leave analytics disabled and produce a server warning. Set MTL_ANALYTICS_UMAMI_ENABLED: "false" and restart to disable it. Newly loaded pages then receive disabled configuration. Already open pages need a reload. No frontend rebuild is needed when changing the settings. The public /mtl/api/analytics/umami-config endpoint returns only the effective settings and is not cached. The server permits the configured script origin in its content security policy only when analytics is active. The tracker loads once, asynchronously after page load, and handles navigation within the app. Failed configuration requests or a blocked/unavailable tracker do not block the app. This includes a missing configuration endpoint, a missing script, DNS/network failures and a script request that never finishes. Analytics runs after app mount; authentication, navigation and app interactions do not wait for it. A missing window.umami is ignored. The server validates settings locally without contacting the analytics server. Pageviews use Umami's default anonymous visitor and session identification. The client supplies no Distinct ID or login reference, calls no identify method and stores no custom analytics ID in local or session storage. Pageviews retain one event per route change. Before sending, dynamic URLs are grouped as /mtl/track/:id, /mtl/plan/:id, /mtl/review/:id and /mtl/admin/:section. The same request carries track_id, plan_id, source_id or admin_section in its data object. These values are strings; titles, coordinates and query parameters are not added. Internal referrer URLs use the same grouping. The browser URL and navigation do not change, and grouping adds no requests or custom events. Routes without a parameter keep their own URL. Query parameters and fragments are excluded. Do Not Track prevents the tracker from loading and blocks analytics payloads. The About panel shows an analytics notice when it is configured. The installed user and administration guide follows the same optional setting. Its local guide-analytics.js loader checks /mtl/api/analytics/umami-config after page load. Disabled, incomplete or unavailable settings load no external tracker. Enabled guide pages use the configured tracker and website ID with Umami's default identification. Each HTML guide page records one pageview; query parameters and fragments are excluded, and Do Not Track prevents tracking. Configuration and tracker failures never block guide navigation. The guide does not read login tokens or store analytics IDs. The public website guide uses site-analytics.js and the same default identification; see website generation . See Umami metric definitions , tracker options and single-page apps .

title: Documentation authoring
text: # Documentation authoring Write public documentation under documentation/ and internal material in the separate private checkout under ../mtl-explorer-private/docs-my/. Choose the audience first. Use named pages for small topics; group several related articles when a shared overview helps. Do not add a folder for one article. Start with the documentation index . Internal work starts at ../mtl-explorer-private/docs-my/README.md. Every topic folder has a short README.md with reading order and child links. Each page has one title and short, plain language. User pages describe actions, results, limits, and recovery. Technical pages describe current contracts and link to source. Keep one authoritative source per subject. Link to detailed reference pages. Keep README, markup, and agent notes concise. Keep the root README.md GitHub-friendly, using tables, badges, and collapsibles where helpful. When moving a page, update its references and remove the old file. Do not leave redirect placeholders. Keep proposals and dated verification out of current architecture. Update user guides only when a change affects what the user does. OpenAPI remains the source for API types. Private proposals, operations, research, and dated evidence belong in the separate private repository. For major user-facing features, update the feature catalog when warranted. When the database schema changes, update database architecture and the Mermaid sources and rendered diagrams in database assets , then regenerate public documentation. For each behavior change, check the owning user task (when it changes a user action), administration settings, architecture contract, feature catalog, and current regression checklist. Compare UI labels with components, defaults with shipped configuration, and API fields with the live schema. Update current-status notes in affected proposals; retain dated outcomes and released guides. Include a guide-content review in release preparation, then regenerate and run the checks below. Generate the website and installed guide from the same sources. Edit Markdown, not generated output. Check target paths, fragments, navigation, private links, and freshness before publication. The documentation generator's CLI and version rules are described in the tooling notes . Keep release scope visible in the generated documentation. Keep compact WebP screenshots near their owning topic. Raw captures and bulky datasets go to the mounted external drive. Use public or synthetic data only. The current guide version is CURRENT_GUIDE_VERSION in the generator. Its release note's publication date supplies the Released/Development label. When starting a new version with changed workflows, preserve the previous released guide under versions/<version>/ using the public release snapshot, then update that constant. Keep the installed guide generated from the same current user/admin sources. Topic rules apply to source folders. Generated index.html folders provide website routes; they are not extra topic layers.

title: Generate and check the website
text: # Generate and check the website The product introduction and feature tours live in docs/. Documentation is generated from the audience folders in documentation/; the installed guide uses the same sources. The homepage update link, news, and docs/releases/ are generated from the versioned release notes . Edit those Markdown files, not generated pages or marked homepage/sitemap regions. These helpers do not publish anything. The same generation writes docs/releases/releases.json from published notes and the verified image catalog. Drafts stay out of update offers. See the publication and E2E flow . Shared colors and six text-size roles live in docs/site-theme.css. Reuse those tokens in homepage, guide, and release styles; reserve blue for actions and accents. The installed guide loads documentation/tools/website/guide-theme.js before its styles to follow the app's saved theme. Dark guide colors live in documentation.css; print output uses the light palette. Guide navigation uses compact desktop rows and larger mobile targets. The topic menu and article outline collapse below 960px. Edit the shared layout in generate_documentation.py, documentation.css, and documentation.js, then regenerate both outputs. App guide links retain the same-origin app tab as their opener. The installed guide-navigation.js returns to that running tab and closes the guide on Back to app . Direct guide visits use the app link as a fallback. Links outside the guide open separately without access to the app tab. In an active Python virtual environment, install the release generator's dependency, then generate and check the pages: python3 documentation/tools/build.py docs regenerates the guide and checks release-page freshness. Regenerate release pages with generate_releases.py after editing release notes. Use build.py docs --check to check both outputs without writing. The memory check requires the Docker Compose CLI but does not start containers. It compares service limits, paired tuning settings, and the memory guide's Compose example with the shipped templates. Generation reads the explicit teaser: >- metadata field for banner, news, archive summaries, and release-page descriptions. It inserts that same teaser below the H1 in full website and GitHub notes. Teasers are plain text, limited to 160 characters; see the authoring convention . The news headline and banner identify the version independently of chapter order. The banner sits above the homepage hero and links to the full notes. A null publication date means Upcoming; the latest published release is selected by date and version. Generated output is committed with its Markdown source. The mirror publisher refreshes this output before copying the site and prepares the same teaser and Markdown body for GitHub Releases without metadata. Use the same virtual environment when running ../mtl-explorer-private/publish-to-github.py. With the preview running, check its HTML against the working copy: The check covers canonicals, old-domain references, unique metadata, H1/main, JSON-LD, breadcrumbs, image dimensions, local resources/fragments, sitemap, robots, and navigation reachability. --base-url additionally reads the HTML, sitemap, and robots over HTTP and compares their bytes with local files. It does not fetch every asset or verify external links, indexing, or rich-result eligibility. The offline check is the default. Synthetic GPX examples are generated by generate_examples.py. See the example notes . Real screenshots of year filters use the public demo dataset; see the capture notes . Segment screenshots were captured on 6 September 2026 with public demo routes in an isolated local backend; see the capture notes . Google Health images are real app captures with synthetic data; see their source notes . Capture from the current app through the Codex in-app browser, using public or fully synthetic data. Keep raw captures on the external drive. With Pillow available, encode the two JPEG captures at the website's four WebP sizes: The helper preserves screenshot content and aspect ratio, never upscales, and reports dimensions and byte sizes. Match HTML dimensions and srcset widths to that output; update image cache versions and source notes when replacing captures. When a release is explicitly requested, use ../mtl-explorer-private/publish-to-github.py and then run the read-only check against https://mtl-explorer.com/. Inspect Search Console separately for the selected canonicals and the sitemap's successful read. Product tours, release pages and every generated public documentation page load analytics from docs/site-analytics.js. The installed app guide instead loads guide-analytics.js, which follows the application's optional Umami configuration. The page's hostname selects the configuration automatically: | Page hostname | Tracker host | Umami website ID | | --- | --- | --- | | mtl-explorer.com | stats.mtl-explorer.com | eb0877dd-d24d-4a5d-8735-eaeed78f0f38 | | localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1] (any port) | umami.me.mindalyze.com | c221b96a-f9e6-4f6a-b272-2f6649371876 | | Other hostnames or files opened directly | Disabled | — | The preview command above uses the test website. Publishing the same files at mtl-explorer.com uses production automatically. The tracker starts asynchronously after window load and respects Do Not Track in both environments. Page code does not wait for analytics. Query strings and fragments are excluded, including campaign query parameters. There are no custom click events or tracking-dependent navigation. The website and installed guide use Umami's default anonymous visitor and session identification. They supply no Distinct ID and create no custom identifier in local or session storage. Generated public documentation links to the homepage's Site analytics notice. When changing tracking, verify the selected host and website ID in both environments, then check a blocked/hanging script and a failed/hanging collector in a browser. Pages must finish loading and their links and screenshot controls must work in every case. Intercept test submissions so local verification does not add synthetic visits to the live analytics database. Component release previews: add --components to prepare_update_preview. Release manifests and ownership settings: release updates .

title: Documentation screenshots
text: # Documentation screenshots Use real app captures with public or fully synthetic data. Prefer compact WebP; use PNG only when needed. Keep raw images and recordings on the mounted external drive. Record the app/build, dataset source, workflow, and capture date with the topic or evidence. Keep visible controls and labels readable. Include compact captures for working functions in full regression reports. Reuse existing validated assets where they describe the current flow. Feature capture notes and Health capture notes record their origins. The Health image helper encodes established screenshot sizes without changing the content. Update dimensions, source notes, and image references together.

title: User documentation style
text: # User documentation style Applies to the README, the website, and the installation, administration, and user guide pages, which also become the guide inside the app. It also applies to text in the app itself: help panels, info icons, and status messages. Keep their wording consistent with the guide, and use the same names as the menus. ## The test Keep a sentence only if it helps the reader do something, understand a result, or decide whether MTL Explorer is right for them. Drop details the reader already sees on screen or never needs. Background and story pages, such as Why I built MTL Explorer , are exempt: they may be personal and narrative, but still in plain language. ## Write - Write for someone installing or using MTL Explorer, not a developer. - Address the reader as "you". Use active verbs and short sentences. - Start with the goal, then the steps, then what the reader will see. - Number steps. Bold UI labels exactly as shown: Settings → Processing . - Use plain words: "folder", not "mount"; "service", not "sidecar". Explain a technical term the first time it appears. - Put warnings first and in bold. - Link to details instead of repeating them. ## Leave out | Content | Where it belongs | | --- | --- | | Panel sizes, layout, animation, scrolling, focus | Nowhere; users see it | | Edge cases, internal states, retries, timing | Architecture | | Server internals: memory tuning, database, API fields | Architecture or Development | | What changed, was removed, or was renamed | Release notes | | Developer and test-only steps | Development | ## Page shape 1. Title names the task: "Import GPS files". 2. One sentence on what it does for the reader. 3. Steps. 4. Optional: "If something goes wrong". ## Examples Before: "Opening a photo or video keeps the GPS panel at its current size underneath. Outside map exploration, the viewer keeps its own panel sizes…" After: delete it; the user sees this. Before: "Allow the images to download and the database to initialize. Startup time depends on the host, network, and existing service data." After: "The first start downloads the images and sets up the database. This can take several minutes."

title: Features
text: # Features MTL Explorer keeps your GPS tracks, photos, videos, and optional health data on your own server. This list describes the version in development; see the released guides for older versions. | Topic | What you can do | Guide | | --- | --- | --- | | Import | Upload files or copy them into a folder; GPX, FIT, and six other formats; optional Garmin download; files added while the server was off are picked up | Import tracks | | Map | See all your tracks on one map; click any spot to see tracks, photos, places, and public trails there; choose base maps, trail and place layers, and a heatmap | Map | | Filters | Choose tracks by date, activity, and other criteria; group and color them; write your own filters in SQL | Filters | | Tracks | Search and sort your tracks; see summaries, graphs, related tracks, data quality, photos, breaks and GPS gaps; download the original file | Tracks | | Review | Check files with problems, look at the original GPS points, fix files in another tool, and choose whether a track counts on the map, in statistics, or both | Review | | Statistics | Totals, activity types, highlights, trends over time, photo counts, milestones, and the tracks behind each number | Statistics | | Energy and motion | Estimated calories, work, and power; training load; moving, stopped, and unknown time; breaks | Analysis | | Exploration | See how much of an activity was new ground compared with your earlier tracks | Milestones and exploration | | Segments | Mark a stretch with checkpoints, find every time you passed it, and compare or replay your attempts, including heart rate | Segment discovery , comparison | | Replay | Replay one activity in 3D, race several attempts, or animate your archive over time | Replay | | Planning | Plan routes on the map with live distance, climb, and elevation; undo and redo; save plans and places; export GPX | Planning | | Media | Browse photos by map, activity, or period; full-screen viewer; download originals; correct camera time; set locations; play videos, converting them when your browser needs it | Photos and videos | | Health | Optional read-only copy of your Google Health data: trends, records, exercise routes, and heart rate on tracks | Health | | Preferences | Theme, date and number format, units, and signing out with or without clearing local data | Settings | | Mobile and offline | Use it on your phone, show your position, install it as an app, and view already loaded tracks and maps offline | Mobile and offline | | Administration | Data folders, import progress, rescans, logs, component versions, update checks, backups, and updates | Administration , Logs | ## Limits - MTL Explorer can't add data your files don't have, such as missing timestamps or elevation. - Energy and exploration are estimates. - Duplicates, and tracks excluded from statistics in Review, don't count there. - Route planning needs downloaded routing data. Online maps, 3D terrain, and trail layers need the internet. - Offline, you only see what this browser already loaded. MTL Explorer does not record activities. - Google Health is in beta and needs your own Google API access. Its dates are separate from the track filter. - Photo counts follow the time span of your filtered tracks and the All media / Track related choice. ## Demo The public demo uses public Porto taxi tracks and generated data . Its health data is made up. You can't connect a Google account in the demo. For how things work inside, see Architecture . For building and testing, see Development .
